pages.name: ProgressRing
pages.content:
---
title: ProgressRing
description: Show measured or indeterminate progress in a compact circular indicator.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import ProgressRingReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/feedback/progress-ring.mdx';

## Overview

`ProgressRing` supplies a circular appearance for [Progress](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress). It shares the root's custom range, null, formatting, labeling, native prop, ref, and render contract. Optional children display a preformatted value beside the ring.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-progressring-progressring--display"
  title="Progress ring example"
  height={90}
/>

## Usage

Supply the raw controlled value and an accessible name. Use `aria-valuetext` when a formatted value explains progress more clearly than a percentage.

```tsx
import { ProgressRing } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/feedback';

export const ImportProgress = () => (
  <ProgressRing
    value={600}
    max={1000}
    aria-label="Importing records"
    aria-valuetext="600 of 1,000 records"
  >
    600 / 1,000
  </ProgressRing>
);
```

Use `aria-labelledby` to associate the ring with an existing visible label, or compose `Progress.Label` as a child. Preformatted children do not automatically provide the ring's accessible name.

## Controlled progress and ranges

The application calculates `value` and formats display content. The ring does not fetch data, advance progress, or calculate quotas. `min` defaults to `0`, and `max` defaults to `100`. Finite values are clamped to the range for semantic values and arc geometry. The arc fills by the normalized percentage, including when the minimum is nonzero.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-progressring-progressring--custom-range"
  title="Circular progress in a custom range"
  height={90}
/>

Pass `value={null}` for indeterminate progress. The ring omits `aria-valuenow` and displays an indeterminate arc. Non-finite values also remain indeterminate; they do not become zero or completion. Display content stays controlled by the application.

Use `locale`, `format`, and `getAriaValueText` as described in [Progress](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress). Compose `Progress.Value` to display the root's formatted value.

Use [ProgressBar](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress-bar) for horizontal progress or [MetricRow](/ui/components/data-display/metric-row) for a label and aligned value.

## Appearance and composition

`size="md"` renders a 16px ring; `size="sm"` renders a 14px ring. Both use a 2px stroke and fill clockwise from the top. `barColor` accepts CSS colors, including theme variables. The SVG is decorative and hidden from accessibility APIs.

Value changes animate for 300ms. Reduced-motion preferences disable the transition and indeterminate rotation. Native attributes, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the outer progress element. `className` and `style` can receive the progress state. `render` can replace the root while retaining its semantics.

## Props

<ProgressRingReference />

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-usage-limits" />

props.name: aria-labelledby

props.name: barColor
props.description: CSS color of the filled arc. Defaults to the blue theme color.

props.name: children

props.name: className

props.name: format

pages.name: DetailsRow
pages.content:
---
title: DetailsRow
description: Align detail labels with wrapping values and optional actions.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import DetailsRowReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/data-display/details-row.mdx';

## Overview

`DetailsRow` pairs a label with a value in a description list. Add a decorative icon, multiple value items, or an action supplied by your application.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-data-display-detailsrow--display"
  title="Details row example"
  height={220}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { DetailsRow } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';
import { IconNotes, IconTag, IconUser } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { Chip, Tag } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/data-display';
import { Card } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

export const CollectionDetails = () => (
  <Card.Root>
    <Card.Content>
      <dl style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, margin: 0 }}>
        <DetailsRow label="Owner" startIcon={<IconUser size={16} />}>
          <Chip>Jordan Lee</Chip>
        </DetailsRow>
        <DetailsRow label="Categories" startIcon={<IconTag size={16} />}>
          <Tag color="blue">Research</Tag>
          <Tag color="purple">Design</Tag>
        </DetailsRow>
        <DetailsRow label="Description" startIcon={<IconNotes size={16} />}>
          A shared collection of customer research and design decisions.
        </DetailsRow>
      </dl>
    </Card.Content>
  </Card.Root>
);
```

Place each row directly inside a `dl`. Pass the label through `label` and its value through `children`. The application owns labels, localization, formatted values, and placeholders for missing values.

## Alignment and wrapping

Labels and values wrap rather than truncate. Multiple value items, such as chips or tags, wrap onto additional lines. Rows align their content at the top as that content grows.

The label column defaults to `7rem` and is capped at 40% of the row's width to leave space for the value in narrow containers. Set the same `labelWidth` on sibling rows to adjust their alignment. Numbers use pixels; CSS lengths such as `'8rem'` are also supported.

```tsx
import { DetailsRow } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';

export const PublicationDetails = () => (
  <dl style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, margin: 0, maxWidth: 360 }}>
    <DetailsRow label="Primary contributor" labelWidth={128}>
      Jordan Lee
    </DetailsRow>
    <DetailsRow label="Review notes" labelWidth={128}>
      Include findings from the customer interviews before publication.
    </DetailsRow>
  </dl>
);
```

## Actions

Use `action` for a control beside the value. The row does not add editing, click, or keyboard behavior. Supply a control with an accessible name and connect its handler to the application behavior.

```tsx
import { DetailsRow } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';
import { LightIconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconCopy } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const ContactDetails = ({ onCopy }: { onCopy: () => void }) => (
  <dl style={{ margin: 0 }}>
    <DetailsRow
      label="Email"
      action={
        <LightIconButton aria-label="Copy email address" onClick={onCopy}>
          <IconCopy size={16} />
        </LightIconButton>
      }
    >
      jordan@example.com
    </DetailsRow>
  </dl>
);
```

## Composition and accessibility

Each row renders a `div` grouping with a `dt` label and a `dd` containing the value and optional action. The caller supplies the enclosing `dl`. Provide meaningful text in the label. The optional `startIcon` is hidden from assistive technology, and the caller controls its dimensions.

Native attributes, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the outer `div`. When using `render` with a custom wrapper, preserve that `div` directly inside the `dl` and forward all supplied props and the ref. Keep actions inside their slot so the term and definition remain the row's direct children.

Use [MetricRow](/ui/components/data-display/metric-row) for a metric with optional progress. `DetailsRow` provides only the label, value, and action layout.

## Props

<DetailsRowReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-input" />

props.description: CSS class applied to the row root.

props.name: label

props.description: Preferred label column width. Numbers use pixels. The column is capped at 40% of the row width; use the same width for aligned sibling rows.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the row root div.

pages.name: Shortcut
pages.content:
---
title: Shortcut
description: Display simultaneous key combinations and sequential shortcuts.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import ShortcutReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/typography/shortcut.mdx';

## Overview

Import `Shortcut` and `formatShortcut` from `twenty-ui/primitives/typography`. Both share the same model, symbols, and separators. Register shortcuts in your application. `Shortcut` only formats the hint; it does not register keyboard actions. Native attributes, event handlers, styles, class names, and refs target its outer span. `ShortcutProps` and `ShortcutFormatOptions` are public types.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-shortcut--display"
  title="Shortcut presentations"
  height={90}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Shortcut } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const SearchShortcut = () => <Shortcut shortcut={['Mod', 'K']} />;
```

## Combinations and sequences

```tsx
import { Shortcut, formatShortcut } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const ShortcutExamples = () => (
  <>
    <Shortcut shortcut={['Enter']} />
    <Shortcut shortcut={['Mod', 'K']} />
    <Shortcut shortcut={[['G'], ['P']]} sequenceJoinLabel="then" />
    <Shortcut
      shortcut={[
        ['Mod', 'K'],
        ['Mod', 'C'],
      ]}
      sequenceJoinLabel="then"
    />
  </>
);

const hint = formatShortcut({
  shortcut: ['Mod', 'Enter'],
});
```

A flat array is a simultaneous combination: `['Mod', 'K']` means press Mod and K together. A nested array is an ordered sequence: `[['G'], ['P']]` means press G, then P. Each nested array is one combination, so `[['Mod', 'K'], ['Mod', 'C']]` means press Mod and K, then Mod and C. Use a one-element array for a single key. Both array forms can be readonly.

`Mod` and `CommandOrControl` display Command on macOS and iOS, and Control elsewhere. Explicit `Command`, `Control`, `Alt`, and `Enter` keys also have display labels. Other strings are displayed as supplied. Device detection is safe without browser globals; `platform` optionally overrides it with `mac` or `other`.

Use `sequenceJoinLabel` for localized join text. `combinationSeparator` can preserve a host convention such as `+`. The default text separator is empty on Apple devices and a space elsewhere. `variant` selects `keys`, `text`, or `button`. `visibility="desktop"` hides the hint at mobile viewport widths while `always` remains visible.

Key symbols have readable accessible names. Use `accessibleKeyLabels` to localize individual key names in screen reader output. Supply `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` for a localized name for the whole shortcut, or `aria-hidden` for a decorative hint. Buttons keep their action names and hide their decorative hints on mobile. Menu and list rows keep their hints visible.

## Appearance

Use `keys` for individual keycaps, `text` for an inline hint, or `button` for the compact hint inside an action. These variants only change the presentation.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-shortcut--catalog"
  title="Shortcut appearance variants"
  height={160}
/>

## Migration

| Previous prop                             | Replacement                                                |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Button `hotkeys={['⌘', 'K']}`             | `shortcut={['Mod', 'K']}`                                  |
| ListItem sequential `hotkeys` / `hotKeys` | `shortcut={[['G'], ['P']]}`                                |
| `hotkeysJoinLabel` / `hotKeysJoinLabel`   | `shortcutJoinLabel` on Button, ListItem and Dropdown parts |
| Manual tooltip key concatenation          | `formatShortcut({ shortcut: ['Mod', 'Enter'] })`           |

Flat stored arrays that represent successive key presses need nesting before being passed to `shortcut`: `hotKeys.map((key) => [key])`. Arrays that represent simultaneous keys can be passed directly. Key strings remain literal tokens, so `['Mod', '+']` contains a plus key and `['Space']` contains the Space key; no shortcut-string parsing is required.

## Props

<ShortcutReference />

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-command-menu" />

props.name: accessibleKeyLabels

pages.name: VisuallyHidden
pages.content:
---
title: VisuallyHidden
description: Keep supporting text available to assistive technology without displaying it visually.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import VisuallyHiddenReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/accessibility/visually-hidden.mdx';

## Overview

`VisuallyHidden` renders a visually hidden `span`. Its content stays in the accessibility tree and can supply an accessible name. It accepts native span props, a span ref, and Base UI `render` composition. Import `VisuallyHiddenProps` from the same entry point.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-accessibility-visuallyhidden--display"
  title="Visually hidden example"
  height={100}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { VisuallyHidden } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/accessibility';
import { IconPlus } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

type AddRecordActionProps = { onAdd: () => void };

export const AddRecordAction = ({ onAdd }: AddRecordActionProps) => (
  <Button onClick={onAdd}>
    <IconPlus aria-hidden />
    <VisuallyHidden>Add record</VisuallyHidden>
  </Button>
);
```

Use a visible label when space permits. For controls that already accept `aria-label`, that attribute is another way to supply an accessible name.

## Hidden content

Place supporting text inside the wrapper. Avoid placing focusable controls inside it: the wrapper stays visually hidden when its children receive focus. It does not add a live region, remove content from assistive technology, or hide confidential data.

Use `id` to associate hidden descriptions with `aria-describedby`. Native attributes, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the hidden span or the element supplied through `render`. See [accessibility](/ui/accessibility) for labeling and announcement patterns.

## Props

<VisuallyHiddenReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-accessibility" />

props.name: children
props.description: Content hidden visually while remaining available to assistive technology.

props.name: render
props.description: Element or render function composed with the hidden span props and ref.

pages.name: ColorSample
pages.content:
---
title: ColorSample
description: Display a theme color or a custom color alongside a text label.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import ColorSampleReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/data-display/color-sample.mdx';

## Overview

`ColorSample` is a non-interactive color swatch. Use it next to a label so the meaning does not depend on color alone. Selection belongs to the surrounding control.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-data-display-colorsample--display"
  title="ColorSample example"
  height={90}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { ColorSample } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/data-display';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const PriorityColor = () => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <ColorSample colorName="red" render={<span />} aria-hidden="true" />
    High priority
  </Text>
);
```

`colorName` selects a theme palette entry for the fill and border. `variant` accepts `default` or `circle`. Omitting it uses the default shape.

## Custom colors

```tsx
import { ColorSample } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/data-display';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const BrandColor = () => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <ColorSample
      colorName="blue"
      color="#2563eb"
      render={<span />}
      aria-hidden="true"
    />
    Brand blue
  </Text>
);
```

A custom `color` overrides the fill; `colorName` remains required and still determines the border color. Native props, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the swatch div. `render` accepts an element or callback through Base UI composition, for example a span inside text. Consumer styles override the default fill, border, or geometry. Decorative swatches use `aria-hidden="true"`; a standalone meaningful swatch uses `role="img"` with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. To offer selectable colors, compose the swatch inside a labeled [ListItem](/ui/primitives/navigation/list-item).

## Migration

`ColorSampleProps` and `ColorSampleVariant` remain available from the data-display family. The unused `pipeline` variant is removed. Product-specific indicators belong in the application, using native styles or composition. Default and circle swatches keep their existing appearance.

## Props

pages.name: Skeleton
pages.content:
---
title: Skeleton
description: Show themed placeholder shapes while content loads.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import SkeletonReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/feedback/skeleton.mdx';

## Overview

`Skeleton` provides a placeholder shape with theme colors and a moving highlight. Compose shapes in the layout of the content being loaded. The application owns loading state and feature-specific layouts.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-skeleton--display"
  title="Skeleton shapes"
  height={110}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Skeleton, SKELETON_HEIGHT_SIZES } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/feedback';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const LoadingProfile = () => (
  <Text render={<div />} style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 16 }}>
    <Skeleton width={40} height={40} borderRadius="50%" />
    <Text
      render={<div />}
      style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8 }}
    >
      <Skeleton width={180} height={SKELETON_HEIGHT_SIZES.s} />
      <Skeleton width={120} height={SKELETON_HEIGHT_SIZES.xs} />
    </Text>
  </Text>
);
```

Skeleton renders as a block and never grows wider than its container. Use `layout="inline"` to place a placeholder inside a line of text.

Numeric dimensions use pixels. CSS lengths such as percentages and `em` are also supported. Without dimensions, the placeholder fills the available width and uses the inherited font height. Use equal dimensions and `borderRadius="50%"` for a circle.

`SKELETON_HEIGHT_SIZES` provides shared heights for `xs` (13px), `s` (16px), `m` (24px), `l` (32px) and `xl` (40px). Keep layout-specific dimensions in the application.

Each `Skeleton` renders one placeholder. Keep repeated lines, text-line spacing and loading regions in application components that wrap the primitive.

## Motion and accessibility

Skeletons are decorative and have `aria-hidden="true"` by default. Keep loading announcements in a host-owned status region instead of announcing each shape. Skeleton does not accept children.

The highlight moves from left to right on a 1.5-second ease-in-out loop and is hidden when the user prefers reduced motion. Pass `animated={false}` for a static placeholder.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-skeleton--static"
  title="Static skeleton"
  height={90}
/>

## Composition and theme

Native props, `className`, `style` and `ref` target the placeholder span. Use `render` to compose another element. Explicit native styles override dimension and color props.

The base and highlight colors default to the theme tertiary background and lighter transparent background. Use `baseColor`, `highlightColor` and `borderRadius` to override them. Corners stay round, including when the theme uses squircles. The default radius uses the `smRound` theme token (4px). Pass `themeCssVariables.border.radius.mdRound` from `twenty-ui/theme` for 8px corners. Custom pixel and CSS radii remain supported, including `borderRadius={80}` for a narrow capsule and `borderRadius="50%"` for a circle. No skeleton-specific provider or stylesheet import is needed after loading `twenty-ui/style.css` and the UI theme.

pages.name: ProgressBar
pages.content:
---
title: ProgressBar
description: Show measured or indeterminate progress with a horizontal bar.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import ProgressBarReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/feedback/progress-bar.mdx';

## Overview

`ProgressBar` supplies a horizontal appearance for [Progress](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress). It preserves the complete root contract, including native attributes, refs, render composition, formatting, custom ranges, and indeterminate progress. Give it an `aria-label` that identifies the operation.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-progressbar-progressbar--display"
  title="ProgressBar example"
  height={100}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/feedback';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

type ImportProgressProps = { importedRecords: number | null };

export const ImportProgress = ({ importedRecords }: ImportProgressProps) => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8, width: 300 }}>
    <Text>Importing records: {importedRecords ?? 'preparing'}</Text>
    <ProgressBar
      value={importedRecords}
      max={1000}
      aria-label="Importing records"
    />
  </Text>
);
```

## State ownership and ranges

`value` is required and controlled by the application. There is no `defaultValue` mode. The component does not start a request or advance progress by itself. Pass `null` when progress is unknown. Non-finite values also remain indeterminate.

`min` defaults to `0`, and `max` defaults to `100`. Finite values are clamped to the range for the semantic value and normalized fill. A value of `70` in the range `20` to `120` fills half the bar and reports `50%`, while `aria-valuenow` stays `70`.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-progressbar-progressbar--custom-range"
  title="A nonzero minimum and custom maximum"
  height={80}
/>

Use `aria-valuetext`, `getAriaValueText`, `locale`, and `format` as described in [Progress](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress). Use composed Progress parts when labels and values need their own visible layout.

Use [Toast](/ui/components/feedback/toast) for notifications with a dismiss countdown and hover pause.

## Appearance and composition

`size` selects a 4px, 6px or 8px track. `barColor` and `backgroundColor` accept CSS colors, including theme variables. `withBorderRadius` rounds the track and indicator. `withMinimumFillWidth` keeps a small cosmetic fill only between the minimum and completion. This minimum is at most 12px and half the track width, so a narrow track still distinguishes incomplete progress from completion. It does not fill an empty bar or change semantic values.

Native attributes, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the root. `className` and `style` can receive the progress state. `render` can replace the root while preserving its semantics. Indeterminate progress has its own appearance without reporting a numeric percentage. Reduced-motion preferences disable fill transitions and indeterminate motion.

Compose [Progress parts](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress) for custom layouts or feature animation. Feature timing, grow-in, glints, springs, and completion callbacks belong to the application composition.

## Migration

Replace `ariaLabel` with native `aria-label`. The `withGrowIn`, `withGlint`, `withSpringFill`, and `onGrowInComplete` props are removed. Implement their appearance, timing, and completion callbacks in an application composition using [Progress parts](/ui/primitives/feedback/progress). Native `onAnimationEnd` remains available on the root.

## Props

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-usage-limits" />

pages.name: Collapsible
pages.content:
---
title: Collapsible
description: Compose an accessible trigger and animated panel with controlled or uncontrolled expansion.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import CollapsibleReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/layout/collapsible.mdx';

## Overview

`Collapsible` exposes Base UI's Root, Trigger, and Panel contracts. Root owns expansion state, Trigger supplies keyboard activation and the panel relationship, and Panel owns animation and content lifetime.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-collapsible--display"
  title="Collapsible example"
  height={160}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Collapsible } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/layout';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const ImportDetails = () => (
  <Collapsible.Root defaultOpen style={{ width: 360, maxWidth: '100%' }}>
    <Collapsible.Trigger render={<Button />}>
      Import details
    </Collapsible.Trigger>
    <Collapsible.Panel>
      <Text
        style={{
          paddingTop: 12,
          color: 'var(--t-font-color-secondary)',
          lineHeight: 1.5,
        }}
      >
        Match each CSV column to a record field before importing.
      </Text>
    </Collapsible.Panel>
  </Collapsible.Root>
);
```

Use `defaultOpen` for uncontrolled expansion. Use `open` and `onOpenChange` when the application owns the state. The callback receives the requested boolean and Base UI event details, including `reason`, `event`, and `cancel()`. Canceling a change preserves the current state. An externally controlled panel can omit Trigger when its state comes from another control or application condition.

Triggers inherit Root's `disabled` state and can override it with their own `disabled` prop. The native trigger supports Enter and Space and supplies `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` automatically. Give each trigger a meaningful accessible name.

## Anatomy

```text
Collapsible.Root
├── Collapsible.Trigger
└── Collapsible.Panel
    └── Content
```

## Native customization

Root and Panel render a `div`; Trigger renders a `button`. Each part accepts native attributes, handlers, `className`, `style`, refs, and Base UI `render` composition. Class and style callbacks receive the part's state. Forward all supplied props and the ref from custom render components. Set `nativeButton={false}` when Trigger renders a non-button element.

Public types include `CollapsibleRootProps`, `CollapsibleTriggerProps`, `CollapsiblePanelProps`, the three part state types, and `CollapsibleRootChangeEventDetails` and `CollapsibleRootChangeEventReason`.

## Animation and content lifetime

Panel defaults to `dimension="height"`. Use `dimension="width"` for horizontal expansion and constrain the content's width when needed. `containAnimation` defaults to `true`, clips overflow, and lays content out in a column. Set it to `false` when content needs to overflow during the transition.

Panel's `duration` chooses a theme preset (`instant`, `fast`, `normal`, or `slow`) and defaults to `normal`. Reduced-motion preferences disable the transitions.

Panel unmounts after closing by default. Use `keepMounted` to preserve local content state while hiding the closed panel. `hiddenUntilFound` lets browser page search reveal closed content and takes precedence over `keepMounted`.

## Props

<PageBanner illustration="layout" />

pages.name: Separator
pages.content:
---
title: Separator
description: Separate adjacent content with a horizontal or vertical divider.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import SeparatorReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/layout/separator.mdx';

## Overview

`Separator` renders a `div` with `role="separator"` and an accessible orientation. It uses the Base UI separator contract, including native props, refs, and `render` composition. Import `SeparatorProps` from the same entry point.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-separator--display"
  title="Horizontal separator"
  height={130}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Separator } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/layout';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const ImportSources = () => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--t-spacing-3)' }}>
    <Text>Import records from a CSV file.</Text>
    <Separator />
    <Text>Connect an external data source.</Text>
  </Text>
);
```

## Orientation and appearance

`orientation` defaults to `horizontal`. Margins default to zero in both orientations. Horizontal separators fill the available width. Vertical separators stretch along their flex container. Give a standalone vertical separator a height. Control spacing through the parent layout, or use native `style` or `className` for explicit margins and line color. Base UI also accepts functions of the orientation for these props.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-separator--vertical-documentation"
  title="Vertical separator"
  height={150}
/>

## Labeled dividers

Use [LabeledSeparator](/ui/components/layout/labeled-separator) for a text label between divider lines or at the end of a rule. It provides the layout and a single accessible separator name.

```tsx
import { LabeledSeparator } from 'twenty-ui/components/layout';

export const SignInDivider = () => <LabeledSeparator>Or</LabeledSeparator>;
```

## Migration

Replace the former horizontal helper with `Separator`. Remove `noMargin`, since margins now default to zero. To keep the former default spacing, add `style={{ marginBlock: 'var(--t-spacing-3)' }}`. Replace `color` with `style={{ backgroundColor: color }}`. Use `LabeledSeparator` for labeled dividers, pass the label as children, and rename `textPosition` to `labelPosition`. Replace separators used only for invisible spacing with layout spacing.

## Props

<SeparatorReference />

<PageBanner illustration="layout" />

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class or function of the separator orientation.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Direction of the divider: horizontal or vertical.

props.name: render
props.description: Element or render function composed with the native separator props and ref.

props.name: style
props.description: Native style or function of the separator orientation. Use it for spacing and line color.

pages.name: ResizeHandle

props.name: axis
props.description: Pointer movement axis without `edge`: `y` for height or `x` for width.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial size when the handle owns its state.

props.name: direction
props.description: Physical increasing direction. Omit to follow the horizontal text direction; use `normal` or `reverse` for a fixed physical edge.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables resizing and removes the handle from the tab order.

props.name: dragThreshold
props.description: Physical pointer distance required before resizing starts. Movement below the threshold remains a click. Defaults to 5 with `edge` and 0 otherwise.

props.name: edge
props.description: Physical panel edge. Determines the movement axis and increasing direction, independently of text direction.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum allowed size.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum allowed size.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called for a click without dragging, Enter, or Space.

props.name: onResizeEnd
props.description: Called after a started drag ends, with its final value and whether it was cancelled. Cancellation restores the starting value within the current bounds.

props.name: onResizeStart
props.description: Called once with the first bounded drag value after the threshold is crossed.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the bounded size during pointer or keyboard interaction and with the restored value on cancellation.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Called with the final size after a successful drag or an effective keyboard size change. Cancellation does not commit.

props.name: placement
props.description: Layout mode: `inline` stays in normal flow, `edge` positions the handle on the panel edge, and `gap` sits between panels. Defaults to `edge` when `edge` is set and `inline` otherwise.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: scale
props.description: Pointer scale or resolver sampled at pointer down. Movement is divided by this positive scale; keyboard steps are unchanged.

props.name: step
props.description: Keyboard arrow increment. Pointer movement uses the pixel delta.

props.name: value
props.description: Current controlled size. Update it in `onValueChange` and apply it to the element being resized.

pages.name: DirectionProvider
pages.content:
---
title: DirectionProvider
description: Coordinate directional keyboard and pointer interactions with the document direction.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import DirectionProviderReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/layout/direction-provider.mdx';

## Overview

`DirectionProvider` supplies `ltr` or `rtl` direction to Twenty UI controls. It does not render a DOM element or set an HTML `dir` attribute. Set both the provider direction and the matching document direction.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-directionprovider--display"
  title="DirectionProvider example"
  height={160}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { DirectionProvider } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/layout';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

type DirectionalChoicesProps = { direction: 'ltr' | 'rtl' };

export const DirectionalChoices = ({ direction }: DirectionalChoicesProps) => (
  <DirectionProvider direction={direction}>
    <Text dir={direction}>
      <SegmentedControl
        aria-label="Billing period"
        defaultValue="annual"
        options={[
          { label: 'Annual', value: 'annual' },
          { label: 'Monthly', value: 'monthly' },
        ]}
      />
    </Text>
  </DirectionProvider>
);
```

The host application supplies translated labels and chooses the direction. Direction context affects directional interactions; the HTML attribute handles text and layout. For example, [SegmentedControl](/ui/components/input/segmented-control) reverses horizontal arrow navigation, and [ResizeHandle](/ui/primitives/layout/resize-handle) reverses horizontal resizing.

## Scope and state

Place one provider around the controls that share a direction. Nested providers can override the direction for a subtree; pair each override with a matching `dir` attribute. `direction` is application-owned and defaults to `ltr`, matching Base UI. Children are optional. Import `DirectionProviderProps` from the same entry point. The provider has no DOM target, native props, or ref. The provider does not translate content or choose direction from the locale automatically.

## Portals and layout

Dropdown, Popover, Tooltip, Select, Dialog, and Toast portals carry the provider direction even when their container is outside the element with `dir`. Without a provider they inherit the direction of their container. Keep the provider direction and the trigger's HTML direction consistent. A scoped `ThemeProvider` continues to own the default portal container.

Submenus open toward `inline-end`. ArrowRight opens a submenu in LTR; ArrowLeft opens it in RTL. The opposite key returns to the parent. Explicit `left` and `right` popup placement still mean physical sides. Collision handling can move a popup when space is limited.

Text, indentation, attached button corners, and directional disclosure icons follow reading direction. Supplied icons retain their orientation. `AvatarGroup.overlap` still names a physical edge; the outer avatar does not extend beyond that edge in either direction.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-directionprovider--reading-directions"
  title="Left-to-right and right-to-left layouts"
  height={1260}
/>

## Props

<DirectionProviderReference />

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-directionality" />

props.name: children
props.description: Controls that receive the direction context.

props.name: direction
props.description: Reading direction used by directional interactions. Also set the matching HTML `dir` attribute on the content.

pages.name: OverflowingTextWithTooltip

props.description: Allows the tooltip even when the text is not truncated.

props.name: color

props.name: isFocusable
props.description: Adds an optional tab stop. Native tabIndex and focusable render elements also open the tooltip on focus.

props.name: isTooltipMultiline
props.description: Preserves whitespace and line breaks in the tooltip.

props.name: lineClamp
props.description: Positive integer limiting visible lines, matching Text. Cannot be combined with `truncate`.

props.name: render
props.description: Replaces the default div. Native props, styles, handlers and ref target the displayed text, not the popup.

props.name: size
props.description: Font size from the theme scale. Omitted values inherit; this does not set height.

props.name: text
props.type: string | number | bigint | boolean | ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | Iterable<ReactNode> | ReactPortal | Promise<...> | null | undefined
props.description: Caller-owned text or React content. Non-string content requires `tooltipContent`. URLs stay plain text.

props.description: Theme font weight. Omitted values inherit.

pages.name: OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider
pages.content:
---
title: OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider
description: Choose when OverflowingTextWithTooltip checks truncation for a subtree.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import OverflowingTextTooltipModeProviderReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/typography/overflowing-text-tooltip-mode-provider.mdx';

## Overview

`OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider` sets how every [OverflowingTextWithTooltip](/ui/primitives/typography/overflowing-text-with-tooltip) inside it handles its tooltip. It renders no DOM element.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-overflowingtexttooltipmodeprovider--display"
  title="Overflowing text tooltip mode provider example"
  height={180}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider,
  OverflowingTextWithTooltip,
  Text,
} from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const RecordCell = () => (
  <OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider mode="measure-on-hover">
    <Text style={{ maxWidth: 220 }}>
      <OverflowingTextWithTooltip
        text="Quarterly account review and renewal preparation"
        isFocusable
      />
    </Text>
  </OverflowingTextTooltipModeProvider>
);
```

Hover or focus the truncated label to read its full value. Change `mode` in the Storybook controls to compare when the tooltip is available.

## Modes

- `measure-on-hover`, the default without a provider, checks truncation on pointer entry and focus. A label that fits stays out of the way of a parent tooltip.
- `measure-on-open` checks truncation when the tooltip tries to open. Use it for labels that mount under the pointer, such as a hover overlay, where no pointer entry happens.
- `disabled` renders only the text, without any tooltip parts. Use it for many labels that a user cannot hover, such as content covered by an overlay.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-overflowingtexttooltipmodeprovider--disabled"
  title="Tooltip disabled for a subtree"
  height={90}
/>

Nested providers override the mode for their subtree.

## Props

<OverflowingTextTooltipModeProviderReference />

<PageBanner illustration="section-document-generator" />

props.name: children
props.description: Content whose OverflowingTextWithTooltip instances use the mode.

props.name: mode
props.description: `measure-on-hover` checks truncation on pointer entry and focus. `measure-on-open` checks it when the tooltip tries to open. `disabled` renders only the text.

pages.name: LightIconButton
pages.content:
---
title: LightIconButton
description: Present lightweight icon actions with standard or subtle emphasis.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import LightIconButtonReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/input/light-icon-button.mdx';

## Overview

`LightIconButton` composes [IconButton](/ui/components/input/icon-button) with a ghost surface and a small size. Supply an accessible name and decorative icon content.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-button-lighticonbutton--display"
  title="Light icon button"
  height={100}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { LightIconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconSearch } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const SearchAction = () => (
  <LightIconButton aria-label="Search">
    <IconSearch />
  </LightIconButton>
);
```

Standard emphasis uses secondary neutral text; subtle emphasis uses tertiary text. Explicit child appearance takes precedence over ButtonGroup values, followed by the component defaults. Semantic colors retain their own contrast treatment. Small controls are 24px with a 14px icon; medium controls are 32px with a 16px icon. Compact controls use `size="xs"` and are 20px.

## Visual options

Compare emphasis at small and medium sizes, including selected, loading, and disabled states.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-button-lighticonbutton--catalog"
  title="Light icon button emphasis, sizes, and states"
  height={410}
/>

## State and interaction

Button owns keyboard activation, disabled and loading behavior, refs, native attributes, and render composition. The native default is `type="button"`. Use `aria-pressed` for toggles and `aria-expanded` for disclosures. The application owns these states and can set `color="accent"` to highlight a selected action. Keyboard focus uses the shared focus ring.

Tooltip text is optional and does not replace an accessible name from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Set `href` for a link. For application-owned routing, supply `render`, `nativeButton={false}`, and `role="link"`.

## Updating existing controls

Import `LightIconButton` from `twenty-ui/components`. Replace `Icon={IconPlus}` with `<IconPlus />` children, `small`/`medium` with `sm`/`md`, `accent="tertiary"` with `emphasis="subtle"`, and `testId` with `data-testid`. Replace synthetic `active` and `focus` flags with semantic state and actual keyboard focus.

Replace `LightIconButtonGroup` with [ButtonGroup](/ui/primitives/input/button-group) using `attached={false}` and explicit children. Set `disabled` on unavailable actions, including actions without a click handler. Wrappers and tooltip triggers can remain around each child.

## Row actions

Use a passive [ListItem](/ui/primitives/navigation/list-item) with an `actions` slot for independent controls. Pass one `LightIconButton` directly, or use `ButtonGroup` for multiple buttons. Each button owns its accessible name, click handler, and disabled state. Wrap dropdown triggers directly around the button.

```tsx
import { LightIconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconEyeOff, IconTrash } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { ButtonGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { ListItem } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const RecordActions = () => (
  <ListItem
    actions={
      <ButtonGroup attached={false}>
        <LightIconButton aria-label="Hide record">
          <IconEyeOff />
        </LightIconButton>
        <LightIconButton aria-label="Delete record" disabled>
          <IconTrash />
        </LightIconButton>
      </ButtonGroup>
    }
  >
    Record
  </ListItem>
);
```

A button without an `onClick` handler can remain enabled when a surrounding dropdown owns its interaction. Set `disabled` explicitly for unavailable buttons. Keep independent controls beside an actionable [ListItemButton](/ui/components/navigation/list-item-button) so each retains its own focus and activation.

## Props

<LightIconButtonReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-pointer" />

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name describing the action. Required unless `aria-labelledby` supplies the name.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: ID of the element supplying the accessible name. Can be used instead of `aria-label`.

props.name: children
props.description: Icon content. Decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: className
props.description:
CSS class applied to the element, or a function that
returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: color
props.description: Semantic color of the button. `inherit` uses the surrounding text color for the label, icons, loader, and outline border, with translucent black interaction surfaces. It supports outline, ghost, soft, and link. Resolving solid with inherit throws, including appearance inherited from ButtonGroup and wrapper defaults.

props.name: elevated
props.description: Adds a shadow and backdrop blur. Neutral outline buttons also use elevated surface colors.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: Standard secondary text or subtle tertiary text. Semantic colors and solid surfaces keep their own colors.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: href
props.description: Destination URL. Renders a native anchor when `render` is omitted unless `nativeButton` is explicitly true. Custom renderers retain their own element contract.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a loading indicator and disables activation.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the rendered root is a native button. Defaults to true for custom renderers. The built-in `href` anchor defaults to false; an explicit value takes precedence.

props.name: render
props.description: Caller-supplied root element or renderer. Native attributes, handlers, event details, and refs reach the rendered root. Use `nativeButton={false}` and `role="link"` for a custom navigation anchor. Router integration belongs to the caller.

props.name: role
props.description: Role of the root element. Use `link` for custom navigation renderers.

props.name: shape
props.description: Square or round icon control.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size: `xs` (20px), `sm` (24px), or `md` (32px).

props.name: style
props.description:
Style applied to the element, or a function that
returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Text displayed when hovering or focusing the button.

props.name: tooltipDelay
props.description: Delay before showing the tooltip.

props.name: tooltipOffset
props.description: Distance in pixels between the button and the tooltip.

props.name: tooltipPlace
props.description: Preferred placement of the tooltip relative to the button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual treatment of the button surface. `link` uses compact text styling without a filled surface or border; render composition determines native semantics.

pages.name: IconButton
pages.content:
---
title: IconButton
description: Trigger actions with accessible icon buttons.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import IconButtonReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/input/icon-button.mdx';

## Overview

`IconButton` composes [Button](/ui/primitives/input/button) with a square or round surface. Pass the icon as children and provide an accessible name with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Icon content is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--display"
  title="Icon button with an accessible name"
  height={110}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconSearch } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const SearchButton = () => (
  <IconButton aria-label="Search">
    <IconSearch />
  </IconButton>
);
```

Sizes are `xs` (20px), `sm` (24px), and `md` (32px). The defaults are `md`, `outline`, and `neutral`. Variants and colors match Button. Use `shape="round"` for a circular button; the default shape is `square`.

## Visual options

Compare one visual choice at a time. Use the named tooltip, elevated, and grouped examples for composition.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--catalog"
  title="Icon button variants, colors, sizes, shapes, elevation, and states"
  height={810}
/>

## Accessible names

Use `aria-label` for a name supplied directly on the control. When visible text already names the action, use `aria-labelledby` to reference it instead. At least one naming prop is required.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconSearch } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const LabelledSearchButton = () => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
    <Text render={<span />} id="records-search-label">
      Search records
    </Text>
    <IconButton aria-labelledby="records-search-label" tooltip="Find a record">
      <IconSearch />
    </IconButton>
  </Text>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  title="Icon button named by visible text"
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--labelled-by"
  height={140}
/>

## Tooltip

Add `tooltip` to show text on hover and keyboard focus. Keep `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` as the accessible name of the action. Disabled and loading buttons retain hover tooltips.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconSearch } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const SearchRecordsButton = () => (
  <IconButton aria-label="Search" tooltip="Search records">
    <IconSearch />
  </IconButton>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  title="Icon button with tooltip"
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--tooltip-documentation"
  height={140}
/>

The tooltip defaults to the bottom, with a 1000ms delay and a 5px offset. Use `tooltipPlace`, `tooltipDelay`, and `tooltipOffset` to adjust it. Omitting `tooltip` renders the button directly.

## State ownership

Your application supplies `loading` and `disabled`. Both prevent activation. Loading preserves the square dimensions and accessible label. The button does not track a selected value or set loading automatically after a click. Native keyboard focus follows the browser; use `aria-pressed` when your application owns a toggle state.

## Elevated actions

Use `elevated` to add a shadow and backdrop blur. The default neutral outline button also gains a bordered surface with matching icon and interaction colors. Other variants and semantic colors keep their existing palette.

`elevated` defaults to `false`. It does not change positioning, visibility, or size. The size remains `md` (32px) by default; set `size="sm"` for a 24px control.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconPlus } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const AddWidgetButton = () => (
  <IconButton elevated size="sm" aria-label="Add widget">
    <IconPlus />
  </IconButton>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  title="Elevated icon action"
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--elevated"
  height={100}
/>

Omit `elevated` or set it to `false` to restore the standard appearance. Elevated buttons support the same tooltips, loading states, links, and keyboard interactions.

<StoryEmbed
  title="Elevated icon action with tooltip"
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--elevated-tooltip"
  height={140}
/>

Replace existing `FloatingIconButton` controls with `IconButton elevated`. Pass the icon as children, use native `aria-label`, and map `small` to `sm` and `medium` to `md`. Supply `size="sm"` when the previous control used its default size. Native focus and `aria-pressed` replace synthetic focus and active flags.

`FloatingIconButtonGroup` is removed. Compose ButtonGroup with IconButton for grouped actions, and keep any shared floating surface in your layout.

## Grouped actions

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconPlus, IconSearch } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const RecordActions = () => (
  <ButtonGroup
    aria-label="Record actions"
    size="sm"
    variant="solid"
    color="accent"
  >
    <IconButton
      aria-label="Search records"
      tooltip="Search records"
      variant="outline"
      color="neutral"
    >
      <IconSearch />
    </IconButton>
    <IconButton aria-label="Create record" tooltip="Create record">
      <IconPlus />
    </IconButton>
  </ButtonGroup>
);
```

[ButtonGroup](/ui/primitives/input/button-group) supplies defaults for size, variant, and color, plus adjoining corners. Explicit child props take precedence independently, including `size="xs"`. Individual buttons do not need a position prop.

Keep attached buttons the same size so their edges align. Set the size on the group and let each button inherit it.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--grouped-overrides"
  title="Individual icon button appearance in a group"
  height={140}
/>

## Links and forms

Without a custom `render`, `href` renders an anchor unless `nativeButton` is explicitly true. For a custom navigation anchor or router link, set `nativeButton={false}` and `role="link"`. The renderer can own its destination without an IconButton `href`. Keep `nativeButton` true for a custom native button, and use false for a non-native action element. Explicit nativeButton and role props are preserved. Disabled and loading links cannot activate. Routing stays in the application.

Native button and anchor attributes, event handlers, event details, refs, and render composition pass through to Button. The ref receives the actual root element. Tooltip composition preserves that root and its accessible name. The default is `type="button"`; set `type="submit"` explicitly for form submission.

## Compact and round controls

Use `size="xs"` for a 20px control and `shape="round"` for circular corners. Existing `RoundedIconButton` controls become `IconButton` with `shape="round"`, `variant="solid"`, and `color="accent"`. Map their old `small` size to `xs` and `medium` size to `sm`. Supply icon children and an accessible name.

<StoryEmbed

  title="Round icon buttons in compact and regular sizes"
  height={140}
/>

title: MainButton
description: Present prominent actions with shared design defaults.

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import MainButtonReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/input/main-button.mdx';

## Overview

Use the shared `MainButton` component for a prominent action. It composes
[Button](/ui/primitives/input/button) with a solid surface, elevation, semibold
text, and 12px horizontal padding. Its default color is neutral and size is `md`.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-mainbutton--display"
  title="MainButton example"
  height={110}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { MainButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';

export const SaveAction = () => <MainButton>Save changes</MainButton>;
```

## Visual options

Compare solid and outline appearances across default and small sizes, plus disabled and loading states.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-mainbutton--catalog"
  title="Main button variants and states"
  height={230}
/>

## State ownership

`MainButton` uses Button's state model and adds no state of its own. Your application supplies `loading` and `disabled`; there are no controlled and uncontrolled selection modes. See [Button's state ownership example](/ui/primitives/input/button#state-ownership) for managing an asynchronous action.

## Forms and width

```tsx
import { MainButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';

export const SaveProfile = () => (
  <MainButton type="submit" fullWidth>
    Save profile
  </MainButton>
);
```

Width follows the content unless you set `fullWidth` or provide application
layout styling. Override `variant`, `color`, `size`, and `elevated` as needed;
for example, use `variant="outline"` and `elevated={false}` for an outlined action.

With `color="inherit"`, choose a non-solid variant explicitly or inherit one from ButtonGroup. The standalone solid default with inherited color throws a runtime error.

Keep page layout in your application's styling.

## Interaction

`MainButton` accepts Button's native attributes, event handlers, refs, icon slots,
`loading` and `disabled` props. Buttons default to `type="button"`;
set `type="submit"` explicitly for form submission.

Use `href` for a link. Supply `render` to choose a custom root, including an
application-owned router link. Set `nativeButton={false}` and `role="link"` for
a navigation renderer. Custom native buttons keep `nativeButton` true.

[ButtonGroup](/ui/primitives/input/button-group) can set a shared size, surface,
and color. Explicit child appearance takes precedence over the group, followed by
the component defaults. Consumer classes, including state functions, pass through
to the root.

## Overview

Use the shared `LightButton` component for a lightweight action. It composes

font weight, and no elevation.

## Usage

```tsx
import { LightButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';

export const FilterAction = () => <LightButton>Add filter</LightButton>;
```

## Visual options

Compare standard and subtle emphasis across common action states.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-lightbutton--catalog"
  title="Light button emphasis and states"
  height={230}
/>

## State ownership

`LightButton` uses Button's state model and adds no state of its own. Your application supplies `loading` and `disabled`; `emphasis` only changes appearance. See [Button's state ownership example](/ui/primitives/input/button#state-ownership) for managing an asynchronous action. There are no controlled and uncontrolled selection modes.

## Emphasis and icons

```tsx
import { LightButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconPlus } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const FilterActions = () => (
  <LightButton emphasis="subtle" startIcon={<IconPlus />}>
    Add filter
  </LightButton>
);
```

The default `emphasis="standard"` uses secondary neutral text.
`emphasis="subtle"` uses tertiary neutral text on ghost, outline, and soft
surfaces. Semantic colors and solid surfaces retain their contrast treatment.

Override `variant`, `color`, `size`, or `elevated` when needed.
[ButtonGroup](/ui/primitives/input/button-group) can set a shared size, surface,
and color. Explicit child appearance takes precedence over the group, followed by
the component defaults. Subtle emphasis does not replace the semantic color.

`LightButton` accepts Button's native attributes, refs, event handlers, icon
slots, loading and disabled states, and render composition. Its native default
is `type="button"`. Set `type="submit"` for submission or use `href` for a link.
Supply `render` to choose a custom root, including an application-owned router
link. Set `nativeButton={false}` and `role="link"` for a navigation renderer.
Custom native buttons keep `nativeButton` true.

pages.name: ButtonGroup
pages.content:
---
title: ButtonGroup
description: Group related buttons with shared appearance and an optional frame.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import ButtonGroupReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/button-group.mdx';

## Overview

Give a group an accessible name and place related buttons inside it. The group joins adjacent borders and can apply defaults for size, variant, and color. Buttons retain their own tab stops.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-button-buttongroup--display"
  title="Button group"
  height={100}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { IconCheckbox, IconNotes, IconTimelineEvent } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const ActivityActions = () => (
  <ButtonGroup aria-label="Create activity" size="sm">
    <Button startIcon={<IconNotes />}>Note</Button>
    <Button startIcon={<IconCheckbox />}>Task</Button>
    <Button startIcon={<IconTimelineEvent />}>Activity</Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
);
```

## State ownership

`ButtonGroup` coordinates appearance, not selection. It has no controlled or uncontrolled selection mode. Each button receives its own action handler and application state; see [Button's state ownership example](/ui/primitives/input/button#state-ownership) for loading behavior.

For a mutually exclusive choice, use [RadioGroup](/ui/primitives/input/radio-group), which owns selection for its radio controls.

## Appearance precedence

Each appearance prop resolves independently: the child's explicit prop, then the group default, then the component default. This applies to both Button and IconButton, including an explicit `IconButton size="xs"`. Defaults reach children through fragments, wrappers, and tooltip anchors.

A group can supply `color="inherit"` on a colored surface. A child that resolves to inherited color must also resolve to a non-solid variant. Explicit child color and variant overrides take precedence, so a child may choose a non-solid variant or a semantic color when the group supplies solid and inherit together.

Keep attached buttons at the same size so their edges align. This example overrides variant and color while inheriting the group size.

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const ActivityActions = () => (
  <ButtonGroup
    aria-label="Activity actions"
    variant="solid"
    color="accent"
    size="sm"
  >
    <Button variant="ghost" color="danger">
      Delete activity
    </Button>
    <Button color="neutral">Duplicate activity</Button>
    <Button>New activity</Button>
  </ButtonGroup>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-button-buttongroup--appearance-overrides"
  title="Individual appearance in a button group"
  height={100}
/>

## Detached controls

Set `attached={false}` to keep each control's rounded corners and a 2px gap. Group defaults still apply through wrappers and tooltip anchors; explicit child props take precedence.

## Framed controls

Set `framed` to add a translucent background, border, 2px padding, and concentric corners. The frame works with attached or detached controls and preserves explicit child appearance. Use `size="xs"` on [IconButton](/ui/components/input/icon-button) for compact 20px actions.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-iconbutton--framed-group-documentation"
  title="Framed button group"
  height={100}
/>

```tsx
import { IconButton } from 'twenty-ui/components/input';
import { IconPlus, IconTrash } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { ButtonGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const CompactRecordActions = () => (
  <ButtonGroup framed attached={false} aria-label="Record actions">
    <IconButton size="xs" aria-label="Add" variant="ghost">
      <IconPlus />
    </IconButton>
    <IconButton size="xs" aria-label="Delete" variant="ghost" disabled>
      <IconTrash />
    </IconButton>
  </ButtonGroup>
);
```

## Updating existing groups

Replace `IconButtonGroup` and its `iconButtons` array with `ButtonGroup framed attached={false}` and explicit children. Replace `InsideButton` with `LightIconButton size="xs"`. Each button owns its accessible name, action handler, disabled state, and optional tooltip.

## Props

<ButtonGroupReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-pointer" />

props.description: Join adjacent controls. Set to false for independently rounded buttons with a 2px gap.

props.name: color
props.description: Default semantic color for children without an explicit color. Inherited color requires each child to resolve to a non-solid variant; explicit child overrides take precedence.

props.name: framed
props.description: Add a translucent frame with padding and concentric corners. Button sizes and appearance remain independent unless set on the group.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.description: Default button height for children without an explicit size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Default surface treatment for children without an explicit variant.

pages.name: Field
pages.content:
---
title: Field
description: Connect a form control to its label, description, and validation feedback.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import FieldReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/field.mdx';

## Overview

Use `Field` to group one control with its accessible label and helper text. Components such as [Input](/ui/primitives/input/input) integrate with the field directly.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-field--display"
  title="Field example"
  height={180}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const EmailField = () => (
  <Field.Root name="email" validationMode="onBlur">
    <Field.Label>Work email</Field.Label>
    <Input type="email" required placeholder="you@example.com" />
    <Field.Description>
      We send account updates to this address.
    </Field.Description>
    <Field.Error match="valueMissing">Enter your email address.</Field.Error>
    <Field.Error match="typeMismatch">Enter a valid email address.</Field.Error>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

`Field.Root` manages the control's name, disabled state, and validity. `Field.Label` and `Field.Description` connect their content to the control. Set validation timing with `validationMode`; use `validate` for custom validation.

## Anatomy

Place one control and its supporting parts inside `Field.Root`. This tree shows a field built with the styled `Input` component.

```text
Field.Root
├── Field.Label
├── Input
├── Field.Description
└── Field.Error
```

| Part                                  | Requirement         | Purpose                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                                | Required            | Shares the name, disabled state, and validation with the control.            |
| `Item`                                | Optional for groups | Associates each radio or checkbox with its own label and description.        |
| `Label`                               | Recommended         | Supplies a visible, associated label. An accessible name is always required. |
| `Input` or another integrated control | Required            | Receives user input and connects to the field.                               |
| `Control`                             | Alternative control | Provides an unstyled input when you do not use an integrated control.        |
| `Description`                         | Optional            | Adds persistent helper text associated with the control.                     |
| `Error`                               | Optional            | Shows feedback for a matching validation state.                              |
| `Validity`                            | Optional            | Exposes validity through a children render function.                         |

`Input` and `Textarea` already integrate with the field. Place them directly inside `Root`; they supply the control behavior themselves. Compound controls such as [Select](/ui/primitives/input/select#compose-with-a-field) keep their own root and parts inside the field.

## External errors

Use `invalid` when your application owns the error state. An explicit `match` makes the error message visible.

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

type UsernameFieldProps = { error?: string };

export const UsernameField = ({ error }: UsernameFieldProps) => (
  <Field.Root name="username" invalid={Boolean(error)}>
    <Field.Label>Username</Field.Label>
    <Input autoComplete="username" />
    <Field.Error match={Boolean(error)}>{error}</Field.Error>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

Keep error messages actionable and provide a visible label even when the control has a placeholder.

## Grouped controls

Use `Field.Item` inside a radio or checkbox group to associate each choice with its own label and description. Keep the group's label outside the items. An item can be disabled independently; a disabled `Field.Root` disables every item.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-field--grouped-items"
  title="Field items"
  height={220}
/>

```tsx
import { Field, Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const NotificationsField = () => (
  <Field.Root name="notifications">
    <Field.Label>Notifications</Field.Label>
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="important" style={{ gap: 16, marginTop: 12 }}>
      <Field.Item style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'start', gap: 12 }}>
        <Radio value="important" />
        <Text>
          <Field.Label>Important updates</Field.Label>
          <Field.Description>
            Only messages that need your attention
          </Field.Description>
        </Text>
      </Field.Item>
      <Field.Item style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'start', gap: 12 }}>
        <Radio value="all" />
        <Text>
          <Field.Label>All updates</Field.Label>
          <Field.Description>Every change to your records</Field.Description>
        </Text>
      </Field.Item>
      <Field.Item
        disabled
        style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'start', gap: 12 }}
      >
        <Radio value="digest" />
        <Text>
          <Field.Label>Daily digest</Field.Label>
          <Field.Description>Coming soon</Field.Description>
        </Text>
      </Field.Item>
    </RadioGroup>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

## Native integration and types

Field preserves Base UI validation timing, custom validation, controlled and uncontrolled control values, and value-change event details. `Validity` exposes the validation result through its children function. Integrated controls retain their native form behavior.

`Root`, `Item`, `Label`, `Control`, `Description`, and `Error` forward native props, refs, and `render` composition. Their default elements are a div, div, label, input, paragraph, and div respectively. `Validity` does not render its own element.

Import `FieldRootProps`, `FieldItemProps`, `FieldLabelProps`, `FieldControlProps`, `FieldDescriptionProps`, `FieldErrorProps`, and `FieldValidityProps` from `twenty-ui/primitives/input` for the corresponding upstream part contracts.

pages.content:
---
title: InputGroup
description: Add prefixes, suffixes, and actions around a text input.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import InputGroupReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/input-group.mdx';

## Overview

`InputGroup` gives an [Input](/ui/primitives/input/input) a shared border and optional leading or trailing content. Set `size` on the group to size the container and provide a default for its input. Explicit child size takes precedence over that default; the group still controls the shared layout height.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-inputgroup--display"
  title="InputGroup example"
  height={140}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Field, Input, InputGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const WebsiteField = () => (
  <Field.Root name="website">
    <Field.Label>Website</Field.Label>
    <InputGroup
      startElement={
        <Text render={<span />} aria-hidden>
          https://
        </Text>
      }
    >
      <Input placeholder="example.com" />
    </InputGroup>
    <Field.Description>Enter the domain without https://.</Field.Description>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

`startElement` and `endElement` accept React nodes. Prefixes and suffixes are visual content; the input's submitted value contains only what the user enters.

## Visual choices

Compare prefix, suffix, and combined adornments at both input sizes. The group shares its size with the input.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-inputgroup--catalog"
  title="Visual choices for input group"
  height={300}
/>

## Anatomy

Place the input inside `InputGroup` and keep field labels and messages outside the shared border.

```text
Field.Root
├── Field.Label
├── InputGroup
│   └── Input
└── Field.Description
```

| Part or slot                                  | Requirement          | Purpose                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `InputGroup`                                  | Required             | Supplies the shared border, layout, and size.                            |
| `Input` as `children`                         | Required             | Owns the input value, native attributes, and editing behavior.           |
| `startElement`                                | Optional prop        | Adds a prefix, icon, or other content before the input.                  |
| `endElement`                                  | Optional prop        | Adds a suffix or action after the input.                                 |
| `Field.Root`, `Label`, `Description`, `Error` | Optional composition | Associates a label, helper text, and validation feedback with the input. |

`startElement` and `endElement` are React node props, not separate components. `InputGroup` does not supply a label or manage validation. Give the input an accessible name, either through `Field.Label` or its own labeling attributes.

## Trailing action

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Field, Input, InputGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const PasswordField = () => {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Field.Root name="password">
      <Field.Label>Password</Field.Label>
      <InputGroup
        endElement={
          <Button
            type="button"
            aria-label={visible ? 'Hide password' : 'Show password'}
            variant="ghost"
            size="sm"
            onClick={() => setVisible(!visible)}
          >
            {visible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'}
          </Button>
        }
      >
        <Input
          type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
          autoComplete="current-password"
        />
      </InputGroup>
    </Field.Root>
  );
};
```

Put labels, validation, and value handling on the field or input. Give adornment buttons their own accessible names and use `type="button"` when they should not submit the form. The group supports `sm` and `md` sizes and defaults to `md`.

## Customize the layout

Native props, `className`, `style`, `render`, and `ref` target the layout div. A custom `render` element receives the layout props and children. Keep the supplied ref on that layout element.

Put `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `name`, `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, and the native control ref on `Input`. The group does not manage input state or replace Field label association.

## Props

The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

<InputGroupReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-input" />

props.name: endElement
props.description: Content rendered after the input, such as a suffix or a button.

props.name: hasFocusRing
props.description: Set false to keep the group border unchanged on focus. Defaults to true. Error styling remains visible.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the layout element, a div by default.

props.name: render
props.description: Customizes the layout element. Forward its props, children and ref. Native control props belong on the child input.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size of the layout and default size for inputs that omit size. Defaults to md.

props.name: startElement
props.description: Content rendered before the input, such as a prefix or an icon.
