pages.content:
---
title: NumberField
description: Compose a numeric field with locale formatting, stepping, native forms, and scrubbing.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import NumberFieldReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/number-field.mdx';

## Overview

`NumberField` exposes all seven parts of the installed Base UI Number Field: `Root`, `Group`, `Input`, `Decrement`, `Increment`, `ScrubArea`, and `ScrubAreaCursor`. Import it from `twenty-ui/primitives/input`. It retains Base UI's numeric state, formatting, stepping, event details, and native form integration with Twenty UI styling for the input, group, and adjustment controls.

For the compact preset with fixed formatting and modifier-step defaults, use [NumberStepper](/ui/components/input/number-stepper) from `twenty-ui/components/input`.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-numberfield--display"
  title="NumberField example"
  height={140}
/>

## Usage

`Root` owns numeric state. `Input` is the visible text input. Use `Group` to arrange optional decrement and increment controls around it. Supply content and accessible names for the controls; the primitive does not inject icons or labels.

```tsx
import { IconMinus, IconPlus } from 'twenty-ui/icon';
import { Field, NumberField } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const QuantityInput = () => (
  <Field.Root>
    <Field.Label>Quantity</Field.Label>
    <NumberField.Root name="quantity" defaultValue={3} min={0} max={10}>
      <NumberField.Group>
        <NumberField.Decrement aria-label="Decrease quantity">
          <IconMinus size={16} />
        </NumberField.Decrement>
        <NumberField.Input />
        <NumberField.Increment aria-label="Increase quantity">
          <IconPlus size={16} />
        </NumberField.Increment>
      </NumberField.Group>
    </NumberField.Root>
    <Field.Description>Choose up to ten items.</Field.Description>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

`Field.Label`, `Field.Description`, and `Field.Error` associate with the visible input. Alternatively, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to `Input`. The default `aria-roledescription` is `Number field`; it does not provide an accessible name.

## Values and callbacks

Omit `value` for an uncontrolled field, and supply a numeric `defaultValue` when an initial value is needed. Omitting `defaultValue` starts empty. For a controlled field, pass a number or `null` through `value` and update it from `onValueChange`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Field, NumberField } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const PriceInput = () => {
  const [price, setPrice] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [savedPrice, setSavedPrice] = useState<number | null>(null);

  return (
    <Field.Root>
      <Field.Label>Price</Field.Label>
      <NumberField.Root
        value={price}
        onValueChange={setPrice}
        onValueCommitted={setSavedPrice}
      >
        <NumberField.Input placeholder="Enter a price" />
      </NumberField.Root>
      <Field.Description>
        Last committed price: {savedPrice ?? 'empty'}
      </Field.Description>
    </Field.Root>
  );
};
```

Clearing reports `null`, including when `min` is set. Incomplete drafts such as `-` remain editable without reporting an invalid number. Parseable typing updates the numeric value before the edit is committed. The first step from an empty value starts at zero clamped to the bounds; subsequent steps use the active step amount.

`onValueChange(value, details)` retains the native `event`, `reason`, `cancel`, `allowPropagation`, `isCanceled`, `isPropagationAllowed`, `trigger`, and optional `direction`. Reasons distinguish typing (`input-change`), clearing (`input-clear`), blur normalization (`input-blur`), paste (`input-paste`), keyboard, increment or decrement presses, wheel, scrubbing, and native autofill (`none`). Calling `cancel()` prevents the numeric state update; controlled callers still choose their accepted value.

`onValueCommitted(value, details)` runs on blur after editing, on pointer release after stepping or scrubbing, and immediately for keyboard and wheel adjustments. Clearing commits `null` on blur. Commit details contain `event` and `reason`; they are generic details without change cancellation methods. Focusing and blurring an untouched field does not itself commit a value when no numeric normalization is needed. Explicit rounding options can normalize and commit an untouched value.

## Locale and formatting

Set `locale` and `format` on `Root`. They retain the installed Base UI contract: `locale` accepts `Intl.LocalesArgument`, and `format` accepts `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`. Display formatting is separate from the raw numeric value submitted by the form. The primitive does not force Latin digits, grouping, precision, or modifier steps.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-numberfield--locale-currency"
  title="Locale and currency formatting"
  height={140}
/>

```tsx
import { Field, NumberField } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const AmountInput = () => (
  <Field.Root>
    <Field.Label>Amount in euros</Field.Label>
    <NumberField.Root
      name="amount"
      defaultValue={1234.5}
      locale="de-DE"
      format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }}
      step={0.5}
      smallStep={0.01}
      largeStep={10}
    >
      <NumberField.Input />
    </NumberField.Root>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

Typing and paste use the configured locale and supported format symbols. Blur normalizes the displayed text. Explicit precision or rounding options can also normalize the committed number; without those options, formatting alone does not replace an untouched numeric value with rounded display text.

## Stepping and bounds

`step` defaults to `1`, `smallStep` to `0.1` while Alt is held, and `largeStep` to `10` while Shift is held. The active step applies to buttons, Arrow Up and Arrow Down, wheel, and scrub-area movement. `snapOnStep` defaults to `false`; enable it to snap adjustments to the active step. Home and End select the corresponding explicit bound. Native key handlers can call `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` when the owner needs to override Base UI's keyboard behavior.

`min` and `max` are inclusive. Step interactions stay bounded. By default, typed and pasted values also clamp numerically, with the draft normalized on blur. Set `allowOutOfRange` to accept direct edits outside those bounds and let native range validation or application validation report the problem.

`step="any"` disables native step validation while interactive stepping uses `1` and the configured modifier steps. With a numeric step, provide `min` explicitly when native submission must validate step alignment. The numeric step does not round every typed value to a step.

## Scrubbing

`ScrubArea` changes the numeric value as the pointer moves. It supports horizontal or vertical movement, `pixelSensitivity`, and optional `teleportDistance`. The active step and bounds also apply to scrubbing. Use a visible label as the scrub target while keeping the input available for keyboard editing.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-numberfield--with-scrubbing"
  title="Scrub the width label"
  height={150}
/>

Compose `ScrubAreaCursor` inside `ScrubArea` for a custom cursor during pointer-lock scrubbing. It portals to the document body while active. Base UI falls back to the normal cursor for touch input, denied pointer lock, and WebKit. Set `allowWheelScrub` on `Root` to allow wheel adjustment while the input is focused and hovered; it defaults to `false`.

## Forms and disabled state

`Root` renders a hidden native `input type="number"` for raw numeric submission and native validation. Set `name`, `form`, `required`, `min`, `max`, and `step` on `Root`. `form` can associate the field with a form elsewhere in the document. The default adjustment controls use `type="button"`, so stepping does not submit the form.

`disabled` prevents interaction and excludes the value from submission. `readOnly` prevents changes while keeping the visible input focusable and its form value available. Use a controlled value when the application must reset numeric state; native form reset does not reset it.

## DOM targets and customization

| Part or prop              | Default DOM and ref target                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Root` / `Root.ref`       | The outer `div`                                                                |
| `Root.inputRef`           | The hidden native number input                                                 |
| `Root.id`                 | Associates the visible text input's ID                                         |
| `Group` / `Group.ref`     | The group `div`                                                                |
| `Input` / `Input.ref`     | The visible `input type="text"`                                                |
| `Decrement` / `Increment` | Native buttons                                                                 |
| `ScrubArea`               | A `span`                                                                       |
| `ScrubAreaCursor`         | A `span` portaled to the document body while active; its ref is otherwise null |

Native attributes, `className`, `style`, and `render` target the part receiving them. Input customization applies to the visible control; wrapper customization belongs on `Root` or `Group`. To focus the control, use `Input.ref`, rather than `Root.inputRef`.

Each part accepts an element or callback through `render`, with the corresponding public state type. Forward the supplied props and ref to the appropriate DOM element so editing, focus, labels, and validation keep working. When a stepping control renders a non-button element, set `nativeButton={false}`. `className` and `style` also accept state callbacks. State includes numeric `value`, formatted `inputValue`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `scrubbing`, and inherited Field state.

The public entry points export the props and state type for every part, plus `NumberFieldRootChangeEventDetails`, `NumberFieldRootChangeEventReason`, `NumberFieldRootCommitEventDetails`, and `NumberFieldRootCommitEventReason`.

## Front component renderer

React and Preact sandbox fixtures verify initial locale formatting, localized paste, raw numeric form values, accessible labels, refs, render composition, blur commits, keyboard change and commit details, and pointer change details.

Sequential typing after clearing a controlled localized field currently resets the caret in the renderer: typing `2` and then `3` can produce `32`. A formatted pointer adjustment can also race with blur and leave the visible input showing the previous value. Pointer adjustments report changes, but pointer release does not deliver the corresponding commit callback; later blur can commit with `input-blur` instead. Dragging the scrub area and using its custom cursor are also unavailable in the sandbox. These limitations do not affect ordinary React hosts.

## Props

The reference is generated from the installed public component types. Native attributes and event handlers are also accepted on parts that render elements.

<NumberFieldReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-input" />

props.description: Allows typed, pasted, and autofilled values outside min and max. Native range validation still applies; step interactions remain bounded.

props.name: allowWheelScrub
props.description: Allows wheel adjustments while the visible input is focused and hovered. Defaults to false.

props.name: children
props.description: Composed NumberField parts and supporting content.

props.name: className
props.description: Class applied to this part, or a callback receiving its NumberField state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial uncontrolled number. Omit to start empty; the public type accepts a number.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prevents interaction and excludes the value from form submission.

props.name: form
props.description: ID of the form owning the hidden native number input.

props.name: format
props.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for display and parsing, including currency, units, percent, grouping, and precision. Explicit rounding options can normalize the committed value on blur.

props.name: id
props.description: ID associated with the visible input. Generated when omitted.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Ref to the hidden native number input used for submission and validation. Use Input.ref to focus the visible text input.

props.name: largeStep
props.description: Amount used while Shift is held. Defaults to 10.

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale or locale list used to format and parse numbers. Defaults to the runtime locale.

props.name: max
props.description: Inclusive maximum for stepping and native range validation.

props.name: min
props.description: Inclusive minimum for stepping and native range validation.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the raw numeric value submitted by the hidden input.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the next number or null and change details with the native event, reason, cancellation and propagation methods, and optional stepping direction.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Receives the committed number or null and generic details containing event and reason. Typing commits on blur; pointer steps and scrubbing commit on release; keyboard and wheel changes commit immediately.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Prevents changes while keeping the visible input focusable.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref to the root div, or the element composed through Root.render.

props.name: render
props.description: Composes this part with an element or render callback. Forward the supplied props and ref to the corresponding DOM element.

props.name: required
props.description: Requires a numeric value for native form submission.

props.name: smallStep
props.description: Amount used while Alt is held. Defaults to 0.1.

props.name: snapOnStep
props.description: Snaps step interactions to multiples of the active step. Defaults to false.

props.name: step
props.description: Base amount for buttons, arrow keys, wheel, and scrubbing. Use any to disable native step validation while stepping by 1.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to this part, or a callback receiving its NumberField state.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled raw numeric value. Use null for an empty field.

props.name: children
props.description: The visible input and any increment or decrement controls.

props.name: className
props.description: Class applied to this part, or a callback receiving its NumberField state.

pages.content: --- title: Radio description: Render one option in a mutually exclusive radio group. --- import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx" import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx'; import RadioReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/radio.mdx'; ## Overview `Radio` represents one option inside [RadioGroup](/ui/primitives/input/radio-group). Give each option a distinct `value` and a visible label. The group owns the selected value. ## Usage ```tsx import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; export const ContactMethod = () => ( Email Phone Postal mail (unavailable) ); ``` The `size` prop accepts `sm` or `md` and defaults to `sm`. Use the same size for options in a group. ## Visual choices Compare selected and disabled states, sizes, and the default and card appearances. Use a labeled group of options for an actual choice. ## Complete parts `Radio.Root` and `Radio.Indicator` expose the installed Base UI parts without the styled assembly. Compose them when you need custom content or indicator placement. The callable `Radio` supplies Twenty's radio appearance and indicator for common options. ```tsx import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; export const StorageChoice = () => ( }> ✓ SSD HDD ); ``` Standard radios and `Radio.Root` render a span with radio semantics and an adjacent hidden native input. Card radios render a div. `ref` targets the rendered root; `inputRef` targets the input. `Radio.Indicator` renders a span and its ref targets that element. `render`, state-based `className` and `style`, native attributes and event handlers retain their upstream contracts. The public types include `RadioProps`, `RadioRootProps`, `RadioRootState`, `RadioIndicatorProps` and `RadioIndicatorState`. ## Card options Use `variant="card"` for full-width options with an inset radio indicator. Card radios keep their div root by default. Use `render` to choose another element explicitly. When that element is a native button, also set `nativeButton`. Keep interactive controls outside the card content. Give the group enough width for its content and leave space for the indicator at the top right. A title, icon, and short description help explain each choice. ```tsx import { IconLayoutKanban, IconTable } from 'twenty-ui/icon'; import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography'; const VIEWS = [ { value: 'table', title: 'Table view', description: 'Browse records in rows.', Icon: IconTable, }, { value: 'board', title: 'Board view', description: 'Track progress across columns.', Icon: IconLayoutKanban, }, ]; export const ViewChoice = () => ( {VIEWS.map(({ value, title, description, Icon }) => ( } style={{ fontWeight: 'var(--t-font-weight-medium)' }} > {title} } style={{ color: 'var(--t-font-color-secondary)', lineHeight: 1.5 }} > {description} ))} ); ``` ## Explicit native composition ```tsx import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; export const BillingChoice = () => ( } > Monthly } > Yearly ); ``` The ref targets the composed button. For custom non-button roots, leave `nativeButton` false and forward the supplied render props and ref to the actual element. ## Keyboard and selection Tab enters or leaves the group. Arrow keys move between enabled options and select the focused option. Space selects the focused radio. The installed Base UI radio suppresses Enter selection for both default roots and composed native buttons. Selection and change handlers belong on `RadioGroup`; see its [uncontrolled example](/ui/primitives/input/radio-group#uncontrolled-state) and [controlled example](/ui/primitives/input/radio-group#controlled-state). Radio arrows change selection as they move focus. [Dropdown.SelectionGroup](/ui/components/navigation/dropdown) moves focus with arrows and commits a choice with Enter or Space. `Radio` and `Radio.Root` are generic over the value type. Keep that type consistent with its group. Native attributes such as `aria-describedby` can associate an option with additional help text. ## Props The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

pages.content:
---
title: RadioGroup
description: Manage a single selection across a set of radio options.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import RadioGroupReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/radio-group.mdx';

## Overview

`RadioGroup` coordinates the value, keyboard navigation, and form submission of its [Radio](/ui/primitives/input/radio) children.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-radiogroup--display"
  title="RadioGroup example"
  height={110}
/>

## Usage

### Uncontrolled state

Use `defaultValue` to set the initial billing frequency. The group owns subsequent changes.

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const BillingFrequency = () => (
  <RadioGroup
    name="billingFrequency"
    defaultValue="monthly"
    aria-label="Billing frequency"
  >
    <Radio value="monthly">Monthly</Radio>
    <Radio value="yearly">Yearly</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
);
```

The group's `name` identifies the selected value in form submission. Give the group an accessible name as well as labeling each radio.

### Horizontal layout

Groups use a vertical column by default. Set `orientation="horizontal"` for a row. The prop controls visual layout through `data-orientation`; it does not set `aria-orientation` or change keyboard navigation. Both horizontal and vertical arrow keys retain the existing Base UI behavior, including right-to-left navigation through [DirectionProvider](/ui/primitives/layout/direction-provider).

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const HorizontalBillingFrequency = () => (
  <RadioGroup
    orientation="horizontal"
    name="billingFrequency"
    defaultValue="monthly"
    aria-label="Billing frequency"
  >
    <Radio value="monthly">Monthly</Radio>
    <Radio value="yearly">Yearly</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-radiogroup--horizontal"
  title="Horizontal RadioGroup"
  height={80}
/>

The default gap stays the same in either direction.

## Anatomy

Put each `Radio` or `Radio.Root` inside the group and associate it with a label. Use `Radio.Indicator` to compose a custom indicator. `RadioGroup` and `Radio` are separate exports.

```text
fieldset
├── legend
└── RadioGroup
    ├── label
    │   └── Radio
    └── label
        └── Radio
```

| Part                 | Requirement                 | Purpose                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RadioGroup`         | Required                    | Owns selection, keyboard navigation, and form integration. |
| `Radio`              | One per option              | Supplies an option with a distinct `value`.                |
| `label`              | Recommended for each option | Provides a visible, clickable name for its radio.          |
| `fieldset`, `legend` | Optional grouping           | Groups related controls under a visible heading.           |

Give the group its own accessible name using `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. In the examples below, `aria-labelledby` connects the group to the legend. Each radio also needs its own name. Put selection props on `RadioGroup` and option values on `Radio`.

## Controlled state

Pass `value` and update it with `onValueChange` to own the same billing frequency in React state. Selection belongs to the group, not to individual radio controls.

```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react';
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const BillingFrequency = () => {
  const labelId = useId();
  const [billingFrequency, setBillingFrequency] = useState('monthly');

  return (
    <fieldset>
      <legend id={labelId}>Billing frequency</legend>
      <RadioGroup
        name="billingFrequency"
        value={billingFrequency}
        onValueChange={setBillingFrequency}
        aria-labelledby={labelId}
      >
        <label>
          <Radio value="monthly" />
          Monthly
        </label>
        <label>
          <Radio value="yearly" />
          Yearly
        </label>
      </RadioGroup>
    </fieldset>
  );
};
```

`onValueChange` receives the next value and event details. The generic value type is inferred from the props. Use `disabled` on the group to disable every option, or on an individual radio to disable one choice. Arrow keys navigate and select enabled options; Tab moves out of the group. The installed Base UI version supports both horizontal and vertical arrow keys. RadioGroup adds the visual-only `orientation` prop without changing that keyboard contract.

## Native integration and event details

`RadioGroup` renders a div by default. Native props and `ref` target that element; `render` composes another element and changes the actual ref target. `inputRef` targets the representative hidden input of a child radio, using the selected enabled option or an enabled fallback. The public types include generic `RadioGroupProps`, `RadioGroupState`, `RadioGroupChangeEventReason` and `RadioGroupChangeEventDetails`.

The callback receives the original event details, including the native `event`, `reason`, `cancel()` and `allowPropagation()`. Cancel a proposed change before updating controlled state when the choice should be rejected.

Keep `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` on the group for the existing Base UI form contract. The selected value is submitted under `name`; disabled groups are excluded and read-only groups keep their selection. `form` supports a group outside its owning form. The installed version does not restore group state automatically on native form reset. Reset controlled state from the form's `onReset` handler when your workflow requires it.

In sandboxed front components, put the group inside its owning form. The renderer forwards `required` validation and blocks explicit `form` references, which otherwise resolve across the host document.

[SegmentedControl](/ui/components/input/segmented-control) is a convenience preset assembled from these primitives for a short exclusive choice. It uses radio semantics and requires an accessible group name. Tabs and tab-panel navigation are separate controls.

## Props

The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

---
title: Autocomplete
description: Suggest values while the user types and keeps focus in the input.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import AutocompleteReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/autocomplete.mdx';

## Overview

Use `Autocomplete` for suggestions attached to a text input. The input keeps its caret and keyboard focus while arrow keys highlight suggestions. Use [Select](/ui/primitives/input/select) when the user must choose a value from a fixed list. [Dropdown](/ui/components/navigation/dropdown) remains the higher-level component for menus and pickers.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-autocomplete--display"
  title="Autocomplete example"
  height={360}
/>

## Usage

Pass `items` to `Root` and render them through `List` so filtering updates the visible suggestions. `autoHighlight="always"` highlights the first result whenever the list opens.

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

const FRUITS = ['Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry'];

export const FruitInput = () => (
  <Autocomplete.Root items={FRUITS} autoHighlight="always">
    <Autocomplete.InputGroup>
      <Autocomplete.Input aria-label="Fruit" placeholder="Search fruits" />
    </Autocomplete.InputGroup>
    <Autocomplete.Portal>
      <Autocomplete.Positioner>
        <Autocomplete.Popup>
          <Autocomplete.Empty>No fruits found</Autocomplete.Empty>
          <Autocomplete.List>
            {(fruit: string) => (
              <Autocomplete.Item key={fruit} value={fruit}>
                {fruit}
              </Autocomplete.Item>
            )}
          </Autocomplete.List>
        </Autocomplete.Popup>
      </Autocomplete.Positioner>
    </Autocomplete.Portal>
  </Autocomplete.Root>
);
```

`value` and `onValueChange` control the input text. Use `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled initial value. Open state is independent: use `open` and `onOpenChange`, or `defaultOpen`. `Item.onClick` handles both pointer selection and Enter from the input.

`mode="list"` filters without changing input text on highlight. `mode="both"` also supplies inline completion. `mode="inline"` keeps all items and supplies inline completion; `mode="none"` keeps all items without inline completion. `readOnly` prevents inline completion from changing the input.

## Anatomy

Keep related parts inside a mounted `Autocomplete.Root`. Compose the portal destination, positioning wrapper, and content separately. `InputGroup` optionally groups the input with adjacent controls and anchors the popup to that group.

```text
Autocomplete.Root
├── Autocomplete.InputGroup (optional)
│   ├── Autocomplete.Input
│   ├── Autocomplete.Clear (optional)
│   └── Autocomplete.Trigger (optional)
│       └── Autocomplete.Icon (optional)
├── Autocomplete.Portal
│   ├── Autocomplete.Backdrop (optional)
│   └── Autocomplete.Positioner
│       └── Autocomplete.Popup
│           ├── Autocomplete.Arrow (optional)
│           ├── Autocomplete.Empty
│           └── Autocomplete.List
│               ├── Autocomplete.Item
│               ├── Autocomplete.Group (optional)
│               │   ├── Autocomplete.GroupLabel
│               │   └── Autocomplete.Collection
│               │       └── Autocomplete.Item
│               ├── Autocomplete.Row (optional, with Root.grid)
│               │   └── Autocomplete.Item
│               └── Autocomplete.Separator (optional)
├── Autocomplete.Status (optional)
└── Autocomplete.Value (optional)
```

| Part         | Purpose and native target                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`       | Owns input value, filtering, highlights, and open state. Renders no element.    |
| `Value`      | Reads the input text through children or a render function. Renders no element. |
| `InputGroup` | Groups the input and adjacent controls. Targets a div.                          |
| `Input`      | Renders the combobox input and retains keyboard focus. Targets an input.        |
| `Trigger`    | Opens or closes suggestions. Targets a button.                                  |
| `Icon`       | Contains a trigger indicator. Targets a span.                                   |
| `Clear`      | Clears the input value. Targets a button.                                       |
| `Portal`     | Chooses the destination and mounting policy. Targets its portal div.            |
| `Backdrop`   | Supplies an optional overlay beneath the popup. Targets a div.                  |
| `Positioner` | Owns anchor, alignment, offsets, and collision handling. Targets its div.       |
| `Popup`      | Renders the suggestion content and optional focus behavior. Targets its div.    |
| `Arrow`      | Supplies an optional positioned arrow inside Popup. Targets a div.              |
| `List`       | Renders filtered items. Targets a div with the listbox or grid role.            |
| `Item`       | Renders a suggestion and handles pointer or keyboard selection. Targets a div.  |
| `Group`      | Groups related items. Targets a div.                                            |
| `GroupLabel` | Labels its parent group. Targets a div.                                         |
| `Row`        | Groups a row of items when `Root.grid` is enabled. Targets a div.               |
| `Collection` | Renders filtered items through a function child. Renders no element.            |
| `Separator`  | Separates items or groups visually. Targets a div.                              |
| `Empty`      | Announces when no matching items are available. Targets a div.                  |
| `Status`     | Announces changes such as asynchronous loading status. Targets a div.           |

Rendered parts retain native attributes, handlers, refs, state-based `className` and `style`, and element/function `render` composition from the installed Base UI API. Native props and refs target the part's own element. Custom components must forward supplied props and refs. Public part props and state types are exported from `twenty-ui/primitives/input`, together with Root actions and change/highlight event detail types.

`Autocomplete.useFilter()` supplies locale-aware `contains`, `startsWith`, and `endsWith` matching. `Autocomplete.useFilteredItems<TItem>()` reads the internally filtered collection under Root. Treat that result as read-only.

## Object and grouped items

Items can be strings or arbitrary objects. Use `itemToStringValue` to supply the text used for filtering, completion, and form submission. Objects shaped as `{ value, label }` use their label automatically. Render the same item value supplied through Root; no Twenty-specific item shape or selection equality prop is required. Autocomplete owns text input rather than a separate selected object value.

For grouped data, pass groups with an `items` array. Root preserves the item type for `itemToStringValue` and `onItemHighlighted`. Render each group's filtered children through `Group` and `Collection`:

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

type City = { id: number; name: string; country: string };
type CityGroup = { label: string; items: City[] };

const CITY_GROUPS: CityGroup[] = [
  {
    label: 'Europe',
    items: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Paris', country: 'France' },
      { id: 2, name: 'Lisbon', country: 'Portugal' },
    ],
  },
];

export const GroupedCityInput = () => (
  <Text
    style={{ display: 'grid', alignContent: 'start', gap: 8, width: '100%' }}
  >
    <label htmlFor="grouped-city">
      <Text render={<span />}>City</Text>
    </label>
    <Autocomplete.Root
      items={CITY_GROUPS}
      itemToStringValue={(city) => city.name}
      autoHighlight="always"
    >
      <Autocomplete.Input id="grouped-city" placeholder="Search cities" />
      <Autocomplete.Portal>
        <Autocomplete.Positioner>
          <Autocomplete.Popup>
            <Autocomplete.Empty>No matching cities</Autocomplete.Empty>
            <Autocomplete.List>
              {(group: CityGroup) => (
                <Autocomplete.Group key={group.label} items={group.items}>
                  <Autocomplete.GroupLabel>
                    {group.label}
                  </Autocomplete.GroupLabel>
                  <Autocomplete.Collection>
                    {(city: City) => (
                      <Autocomplete.Item
                        key={city.id}
                        value={city}
                        description={city.country}
                      >
                        {city.name}
                      </Autocomplete.Item>
                    )}
                  </Autocomplete.Collection>
                </Autocomplete.Group>
              )}
            </Autocomplete.List>
          </Autocomplete.Popup>
        </Autocomplete.Positioner>
      </Autocomplete.Portal>
    </Autocomplete.Root>
  </Text>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-autocomplete-collections--grouped-objects"
  title="Grouped object suggestions"
  height={440}
/>

`Item.startIcon`, `Item.endIcon`, and `Item.description` provide supporting content. Compose `Trigger` and `Clear` with Twenty UI [Button](/ui/primitives/input/button) through `render`. `Icon` can contain an icon from `twenty-ui/icon`. Keep `Status` and `Empty` mounted while updating their children so screen readers can announce changes.

## External filtering and server suggestions

Use `filteredItems` when your application owns filtering. It must preserve the flat or grouped structure of `items`. `filter` accepts a custom matching function; `filter={null}` disables internal filtering for results already filtered by a server.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Autocomplete } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

const CITIES = ['Paris', 'London', 'Lisbon'];

export const CityPrefixInput = () => {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const { startsWith } = Autocomplete.useFilter();
  const filteredItems = CITIES.filter((city) => startsWith(city, value));

  return (
    <Autocomplete.Root
      items={CITIES}
      filteredItems={filteredItems}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={setValue}
      autoHighlight="always"
    >
      <Autocomplete.Input aria-label="City prefix" />
      <Autocomplete.Portal>
        <Autocomplete.Positioner>
          <Autocomplete.Popup>
            <Autocomplete.Empty>No matching cities</Autocomplete.Empty>
            <Autocomplete.List>
              {(city: string) => (
                <Autocomplete.Item key={city} value={city}>
                  {city}
                </Autocomplete.Item>
              )}
            </Autocomplete.List>
          </Autocomplete.Popup>
        </Autocomplete.Positioner>
      </Autocomplete.Portal>
    </Autocomplete.Root>
  );
};
```

Keep Root mounted when results arrive asynchronously. Control `open` independently so a response can open suggestions while the input remains focused. A mounted `Status` can announce loading; update `Empty` when the completed response has no results. The parent owns debounce, request cancellation, and stale response protection.

`onValueChange` and `onOpenChange` receive the upstream event details, including `reason`, native `event`, `trigger`, `cancel()`, and `allowPropagation()`. Controlled callers decide which requested updates to commit. For example, ignore the `escape-key` value change to keep a server query, or ignore `input-change` opening until results arrive. `onItemHighlighted` receives the original typed item and its highlight reason. Cancellation keeps the installed Base UI semantics; it does not replace the application's controlled-state policy.

## Input composition and native forms

`Input` accepts `size="sm"` or `size="md"` and uses the same styles as [Input](/ui/primitives/input/input). Compose it with an existing input using `render`. The composed control then owns its look: `Input` adds no Input styles and ignores `size`, but still passes your `className`, native attributes, handlers, ref, and state attributes. Forward them to the actual input element. Render Twenty UI `Input` to keep the standard look.

`InputGroup` provides layout and an anchor without adding input borders. It can contain chips or render an existing wrapper. Use [InputGroup](/ui/primitives/input/input-group) through its `render` prop when the whole group needs input styling, as the grouped object suggestions story does. An `Input` without `render` inside it drops its own border. Give the input an accessible label or compose it with [Field](/ui/primitives/input/field).

Root preserves the upstream `name`, `form`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, and native form behavior. Input's native attributes and ref target its input. `submitOnItemClick` opts into form submission when selecting a suggestion; the default does not submit.

Input preserves Base UI's native IME handling, including composition events and its keyboard confirmation guard.

The installed Base UI version retains an uncontrolled query on native form reset. For a controlled query, handle the form's `onReset` and restore the application's initial value.

## Placement, portal destination, and dismissal

`Positioner` defaults to `side="bottom"`, `align="start"`, and `sideOffset={8}`. It retains the installed Base UI anchor and positioning contract, including element/ref/function/virtual anchors, functional offsets, `positionMethod`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `arrowPadding`, `sticky`, and `disableAnchorTracking`. Configure these on Positioner. DirectionProvider controls logical placement and DOM direction.

`Popup` uses the anchor width as its minimum width. Set its `width` to supply a fixed content width. Its native props, styles, render composition, and ref target the content element independently of Positioner and Portal. Popup's `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` retain upstream focus options. By default, suggestions keep focus in the input.

Configure `container` and `keepMounted` on `Portal`. Omitting the container uses the nearest scoped ThemeProvider destination, then Base UI's parent portal or document body. An explicit `null` waits without rendering until a container is supplied. Element, ShadowRoot, and ref destinations pass through to Base UI. An unresolved ref retains Base UI's parent-portal/body fallback.

The default scoped destination preserves its CSS tokens and color scheme. An explicit destination inherits CSS from its actual DOM scope, so place it inside the intended theme scope or supply those styles there. React context and direction remain available across portals. ShadowRoot targets need the library's CSS and theme styles in that shadow tree.

Arrow keys change the highlighted item while the input keeps focus. Enter selects it; Escape and outside interaction request dismissal using upstream semantics. An outside press can activate the destination control. Higher-level pickers can own a different activation policy in their adapter. Call `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` in Input's `onKeyDown` to skip the built-in handler for a key you handle yourself. Use `event.preventDefault()` as well when suppressing the browser's native action.

`Root.inline` with `open` renders suggestions without the popup assembly. Inline items retain their `onClick` selection callbacks, but the installed upstream component fills the input automatically only when its Popup is present. Handle `Item.onClick` when inline selection should update your controlled text. `Root.grid` and `Row` support grid navigation. These modes retain the upstream collection and rendering APIs.

## Migration

Wrap Popup with `Autocomplete.Positioner` and `Autocomplete.Portal`. Positioner requires the Portal context; inline suggestions omit the whole popup assembly. Move placement, anchor, and collision props from Popup to Positioner. Move `container` and mounting configuration to Portal. Keep width, content styles, native props, handlers, and refs on Popup. Use an explicit `Arrow` child for an arrow.

Inside front components, keep the existing scoped portal policy. This API does not expand renderer portal destinations or geometry, scrolling, and dismissal capabilities; those renderer capabilities have separate ownership. Production picker adapters retain their deliberate activation workflows.

## Props

The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, accessible names, and event handlers are also accepted on rendered parts.

<AutocompleteReference />

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-input" />

props.description:
A ref to imperative actions.
- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the autocomplete after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the autocomplete completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the autocomplete imperatively when called.

props.name: autoHighlight
props.description:
Whether the first matching item is highlighted automatically.
- `true`: highlight after the user types and keep the highlight while the query changes.
- `'always'`: always highlight the first item.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the popup is initially open.

To render a controlled popup, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:

To render a controlled autocomplete, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: filteredItems
props.type: readonly TItem[] | readonly { items: readonly TItem[] }[]
props.description:
Filtered items to display in the list.
When provided, the list uses these items instead of filtering the `items` prop internally.
When `items` is also provided, this array must preserve its flat or grouped structure.
Nullish entries are not supported, as in `items`.
Use when you want to control filtering logic externally with the `useFilter()` hook.

Useful when the autocomplete is rendered outside the form.

props.name: grid
props.description:

When enabled, arrow keys navigate across rows and columns inferred from DOM rows.

props.name: itemToStringValue
props.description:
When the item values are objects (`<Autocomplete.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for both display in the input and form submission.
If the shape of the object is `{ value, label }`, the label will be used automatically without needing to specify this prop.

props.description: Whether the highlighted item should be preserved when the pointer leaves the list.

props.name: limit
props.description: The maximum number of items to display in the list.

props.name: locale
props.description:
The locale to use for string comparison.
Defaults to the user's runtime locale.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the input when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys. The first item can then be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> again from the input, or the last item can be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> from the input.
The input is always included in the focus loop per [ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/).
When disabled, focus does not move when on the last element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd>, or when on the first element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd>.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the popup enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the popup: document page scroll is locked and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

props.name: mode
props.description:
Controls how the autocomplete behaves with respect to list filtering and inline autocompletion.
- `list` (default): items are dynamically filtered based on the input value. The input value does not change based on the active item.
- `both`: items are dynamically filtered based on the input value, which will temporarily change based on the active item (inline autocompletion).
- `inline`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will temporarily change based on the active item (inline autocompletion).
- `none`: items are static (not filtered), and the input value will not change based on the active item.

The `reason` can be:
- `'keyboard'`: the highlight changed due to keyboard navigation.
- `'pointer'`: the highlight changed due to pointer hovering. The event may be a `MouseEvent`
  rather than a `PointerEvent`.
- `'none'`: the highlight changed for another reason, such as typing, `autoHighlight`, the
  item list changing, or the popup opening or closing.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the

pages.content:
---
title: Slider
description: Choose a numeric value or range with draggable, keyboard-accessible thumbs.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import SliderReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/input/slider.mdx';

## Overview

`Slider` supports a single number or an array of numbers for a range. Compose its label, track, indicator, and thumbs inside `Root`.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-slider--display"
  title="Slider example"
  height={120}
/>

## Usage

### Uncontrolled state

Use `defaultValue` to set the initial volume. The slider owns subsequent changes.

```tsx
import { Slider } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const VolumeSlider = () => (
  <Slider.Root name="volume" defaultValue={40} min={0} max={100} step={1}>
    <Text
      render={<div />}
      style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}
    >
      <Slider.Label>Volume</Slider.Label>
      <Slider.Value />
    </Text>
    <Slider.Control>
      <Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Indicator />
        <Slider.Thumb />
      </Slider.Track>
    </Slider.Control>
  </Slider.Root>
);
```

## Visual choices

Compare the accent and success colors at minimum, middle, maximum, and disabled values. The enabled sliders remain interactive.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-input-slider--catalog"
  title="Visual choices for slider"
  height={340}
/>

## Anatomy

Put the track and thumbs inside `Slider.Control`, which handles pointer interaction. This tree shows a single-thumb slider.

```text
Slider.Root
├── Slider.Label
├── Slider.Value
└── Slider.Control
    └── Slider.Track
        ├── Slider.Indicator
        └── Slider.Thumb
```

| Part        | Requirement                   | Purpose                                                         |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | Required                      | Owns the value, bounds, step, and orientation.                  |
| `Control`   | Required                      | Handles pointer interaction and positions the thumbs.           |
| `Track`     | Required for the styled track | Shows the full value range.                                     |
| `Thumb`     | One per adjustable value      | Provides a focusable handle with keyboard interaction.          |
| `Label`     | Recommended                   | Supplies a visible label; every thumb needs an accessible name. |
| `Value`     | Optional                      | Displays the current numeric value.                             |
| `Indicator` | Optional                      | Shows the selected portion of the track.                        |

For a range, add a thumb for each value with its matching `index` and a distinct accessible name. Labels and numeric output stay outside `Control`, so they do not become part of the draggable area.

## Controlled state

Pass `value` and update it with `onValueChange` to own the same volume in React state. The callback receives the next value and event details.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Slider } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const VolumeSlider = () => {
  const [volume, setVolume] = useState(40);

  return (
    <Slider.Root
      name="volume"
      value={volume}
      onValueChange={setVolume}
      min={0}
      max={100}
      step={1}
    >
      <Slider.Label>Volume</Slider.Label>
      <Slider.Value />
      <Slider.Control>
        <Slider.Track>
          <Slider.Indicator />
          <Slider.Thumb />
        </Slider.Track>
      </Slider.Control>
    </Slider.Root>
  );
};
```

Use `onValueChange` to keep the controlled value current during an interaction. `onValueCommitted` handles the final value when the interaction finishes, for example to save it. Both callbacks are also available in uncontrolled mode without taking ownership of the value.

Change details include the originating `event`, the interaction `reason`, the `activeThumbIndex`, and `cancel()`. Commit details use Base UI's generic event contract and do not include change cancellation. A canceled change does not commit.

## Range

```tsx
import { Slider } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const PriceRange = () => (
  <Slider.Root
    defaultValue={[25, 75]}
    min={0}
    max={100}
    minStepsBetweenValues={10}
  >
    <Slider.Label>Price range</Slider.Label>
    <Slider.Value />
    <Slider.Control>
      <Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Indicator />
        <Slider.Thumb index={0} aria-label="Minimum price" />
        <Slider.Thumb index={1} aria-label="Maximum price" />
      </Slider.Track>
    </Slider.Control>
  </Slider.Root>
);
```

Give range thumbs distinct accessible names and an `index` corresponding to their value. `minStepsBetweenValues` sets the minimum gap in steps. The root's generic value type is a number or a readonly array of numbers.

To control a range, store the array in React state and pass it through `value` and `onValueChange`, just as for a single value.

## Keyboard and appearance

Arrow keys adjust a focused thumb by a step. Home and End move it toward the bounds while respecting range constraints. `orientation="vertical"` changes the layout and keyboard direction. Use `disabled` on `Root` to prevent changes.

Set `color="success"` for the alternative palette; the default is `accent`.

The default `thumbAlignment` is `edge`. Pass `center` or `edge-client-only` to override it. Native `className`, `style`, and `render` composition remain available on each part, including state functions.

<Note>
  With `edge` and `edge-client-only` alignment, Base UI 1.8 and 1.9 never
  re-measure a thumb after its `Slider.Control` resizes, and a slider mounted
  while hidden keeps its thumbs hidden once shown
  ([mui/base-ui#5995](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/issues/5995)). React front
  components hit the same issue on their first render. Use
  `thumbAlignment="center"` until a Base UI release includes the fix
  ([mui/base-ui#6000](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/6000)).
</Note>

## Native integration and types

`Slider.Root` infers a number or a readonly numeric array from `value` or `defaultValue`, retaining that type in both callbacks. `SliderRootProps` accepts both by default; use `SliderRootProps<number>` for single-value helpers or `SliderRootProps<readonly number[]>` for range helpers.

Every part has an exported props type in `twenty-ui/primitives/input`: `SliderRootProps`, `SliderControlProps`, `SliderTrackProps`, `SliderIndicatorProps`, `SliderThumbProps`, `SliderLabelProps`, and `SliderValueProps`.

Refs target div elements for Root, Control, Track, Indicator, Thumb, and Label, and an output element for Value. A Thumb's ref targets its visible handle; its accessible name and native form value belong to the nested range input. Use `name` and `form` on Root for native submission, with one input per range value.

## Props

The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

<SliderReference />

<PageBanner illustration="section-apps-config" />

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: ((value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue, eventDetails: SliderRootChangeEventDetails) => void)
props.description:
Callback function that is fired when the slider's value changed.
Receives the new value as the first argument; the originating event is
available as `eventDetails.event`. The value is also reflected on
`eventDetails.event.target.value` for form integration.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the change:

- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'none'` when the change is triggered without a specific interaction

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.type: ((value: TValue extends number ? number : TValue, eventDetails: SliderRootCommitEventDetails) => void)
props.description:
Callback function that is fired when a value change is committed.
Does not fire if the value did not change, or if the change was canceled.
**Warning**: This is a generic event, not a change event.

The `eventDetails.reason` indicates what triggered the commit:

- `'drag'` while dragging a thumb
- `'track-press'` when the control track is pressed
- `'keyboard'` for keyboard input
- `'input-change'` when the hidden range input emits a change event (for example, via form integration)
- `'none'` when the commit occurs without a specific interaction

pages.content:
---
title: Tabs
description: Switch between related panels with accessible tab navigation.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import TabsReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/navigation/tabs.mdx';

## Overview

`Tabs` connects each tab to a related content panel using a shared `value`. Keep values unique within a root. Use [TabButton](/ui/components/navigation/tab-button) for route links and adjacent actions.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-navigation-tabs--display"
  title="Tabs example"
  height={160}
/>

## Usage

Use `defaultValue` to set the initial selection. The root owns subsequent changes.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const RecordTabs = () => (
  <Tabs.Root defaultValue="overview">
    <Tabs.List aria-label="Record details">
      <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="activity">Activity</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Indicator />
    </Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Panel value="overview">Record overview</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="activity">Recent activity</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="settings">Record settings</Tabs.Panel>
  </Tabs.Root>
);
```

`Tabs.Tab` accepts `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `badge`, and a `size` of `compact`, `sm`, or `md` (default `sm`). The remaining props retain the installed Base UI contract. Values are not restricted to strings or numbers. Reference values must use the same identity on their tab, panel, and root. A root value of `null` selects no panel.

### Compact tabs

Use `size="compact"` on each tab for short Input/Output controls inside a card. Compact tabs have a 24px minimum row height, small text, and 4px content padding on each side. The existing `sm` and `md` sizes keep their 40px minimum height. Compact tabs use the same indicator, focus ring, and keyboard activation as the other sizes.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const ToolCallTabs = () => (
  <Tabs.Root defaultValue="output">
    <Tabs.List aria-label="Tool call details">
      <Tabs.Tab value="output" size="compact">Output</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="input" size="compact">Input</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Indicator />
    </Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Panel value="output">Tool output</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="input">Tool input</Tabs.Panel>
  </Tabs.Root>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-navigation-tabs--compact"
  title="Compact Input and Output tabs"
  height={110}
/>

## Anatomy

Place tabs and an optional indicator inside `Tabs.List`. Place their panels alongside the list, all within the same `Tabs.Root`.

```text
Tabs.Root
├── Tabs.List
│   ├── Tabs.Tab
│   ├── Tabs.Tab
│   └── Tabs.Indicator
├── Tabs.Panel
└── Tabs.Panel
```

| Part        | Requirement          | Purpose                                                   |
| ----------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | Required             | Owns the selected value and orientation.                  |
| `List`      | Required             | Groups tabs and supplies keyboard focus navigation.       |
| `Tab`       | One per panel        | Activates the panel with the same `value`.                |
| `Panel`     | One per content view | Displays its content when its `value` is active.          |
| `Indicator` | Optional             | Shows the position of the active tab with themed styling. |

Give the list an accessible name and match each tab's `value` to its panel's `value`. Base UI supplies the tab and panel IDs, `aria-controls`, and `aria-labelledby` relationships.

When you provide a custom `id` on `Tabs.Panel`, set `aria-controls` on the matching `Tabs.Tab` to that same ID. The installed Base UI 1.8.0 implementation requires this explicit relationship. Custom tab IDs are registered correctly for the panel's `aria-labelledby`.

Add one `Tabs.Indicator` when you want the active underline. `List` does not insert an indicator.

## Controlled state and event details

Pass `value` and update it with `onValueChange` to own selection. The callback receives the next value and Base UI event details, including the originating `event`, `reason`, `activationDirection`, and `cancel()`.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const RecordTabs = () => {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState('overview');

  return (
    <Tabs.Root value={tab} onValueChange={setTab}>
      <Tabs.List aria-label="Record details">
        <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Tab value="activity" badge={3}>
          Activity
        </Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Indicator />
      </Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Panel value="overview">Company and contact details.</Tabs.Panel>
      <Tabs.Panel value="activity">Recent calls and emails.</Tabs.Panel>
    </Tabs.Root>
  );
};
```

User activation has reason `none`. In uncontrolled roots, automatic fallback can have reason `initial`, `disabled`, or `missing`. Automatic fallback may select `null` when no enabled tab remains. These automatic changes cannot be canceled. Controlled roots keep selection under the application's ownership.

Cancel a user change before updating controlled state, or use the same callback with an uncontrolled root:

```tsx
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const ProtectedTabs = () => (
  <Tabs.Root
    defaultValue="overview"
    onValueChange={(value, details) => {
      if (value === 'restricted') {
        details.cancel();
      }
    }}
  >
    <Tabs.List aria-label="Account sections">
      <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="restricted">Restricted</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Indicator />
    </Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Panel value="overview">Account details.</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="restricted">Restricted content.</Tabs.Panel>
  </Tabs.Root>
);
```

## Keyboard activation, orientation, and direction

`Tabs.List` uses manual activation by default (`activateOnFocus={false}`). Arrow keys move focus; Enter or Space activates the focused tab. Set `activateOnFocus` to select a tab when keyboard focus reaches it. Both policies work with controlled and uncontrolled state.

```tsx
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const SettingsTabs = () => (
  <Tabs.Root defaultValue="profile" orientation="vertical">
    <Tabs.List aria-label="Settings" activateOnFocus loopFocus={false}>
      <Tabs.Tab value="profile">Profile</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="billing" disabled>
        Billing
      </Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tabs.Tab>
      <Tabs.Indicator />
    </Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Panel value="profile">Profile settings.</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="billing">Billing settings.</Tabs.Panel>
    <Tabs.Panel value="notifications">Notification settings.</Tabs.Panel>
  </Tabs.Root>
);
```

Horizontal lists use Left and Right; vertical lists use Up and Down. Home and End focus the first and last enabled tabs. Disabled tabs are skipped. `loopFocus` defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to stop at either boundary.

Use [DirectionProvider](/ui/primitives/layout/direction-provider) for RTL keyboard direction and `dir="rtl"` on the root for layout. Set `orientation="vertical"` on `Root` for a vertical list and indicator.

## Panel lifetime

Use `keepMounted` when panel contents must retain their state while inactive. Inactive mounted panels remain hidden and do not occupy layout space.

## Panel layout

`Panel` fills the space left by the list and can shrink below its content on both axes, so it stays within a root of fixed height. To scroll its content, set `overflow: auto` on the panel, or on a child that fills it, such as a `flex: 1` child of a column flex panel.

## Native props, render composition, and refs

All five parts preserve native props, event handlers, refs, and Base UI `render` composition. Their `className` and `style` can also be functions of the part's state. The default elements are a `div` for Root, List, and Panel, a `button` for Tab, and a `span` for Indicator. Refs point to the actual rendered elements.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { Tabs } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/navigation';

export const ComposedTabs = () => {
  const panelRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);

  return (
    <Tabs.Root defaultValue="overview" render={<section />}>
      <Tabs.List aria-label="Account details">
        <Tabs.Tab value="overview" nativeButton render={<button />}>
          Overview
        </Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Indicator render={<span data-testid="active-indicator" />} />
      </Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Panel
        value="overview"
        render={<article />}
        ref={(element) => {
          panelRef.current = element;
        }}
      >
        Account details.
      </Tabs.Panel>
    </Tabs.Root>
  );
};
```

Keep `nativeButton` consistent with the element composed for a tab. Use `nativeButton={false}` for a custom interactive element that is not a native button and forwards the supplied props and ref. A route anchor belongs in `TabButton`, where the route owns navigation and `aria-current`.

## Visual emphasis

Use `highlighted` on `Tabs.Tab` to outline its content independently of selection, such as when its settings are open. Selection remains owned by `Tabs.Root`.

## Props

The generated reference includes the public props for every part. Public part state types and Root change detail/reason types are available from `twenty-ui/primitives/navigation`.

<TabsReference />

## Migration

Add an explicit `Tabs.Indicator` to lists that should retain the active underline. Remove duplicate indicators from compositions that previously relied on `List` inserting one. Keep route links, create controls, and overflow controls outside `Tabs.List`, whose children select related panels.
