---
title: Dialog
description: Present a focused task above the current page.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import DialogReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/surfaces/dialog.mdx';

## Overview

Use `Dialog` for forms, details, and other tasks that open above the page. It manages focus, keyboard dismissal, outside clicks, and scrolling. Use [AlertDialog](/ui/primitives/surfaces/alert-dialog) when the user must explicitly respond to a decision.

This API is for standalone Twenty UI and the Twenty host application. Front components must use the SDK's [`openCommandConfirmationModal`](/developers/extend/apps/layout/front-components#host-communication-api) instead of rendering `Dialog` or `AlertDialog` directly. Native browser dialogs and popovers are also prohibited in the front component renderer.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-surfaces-dialog--display"
  title="Dialog example"
  height={440}
/>

## Usage

### Uncontrolled state

`Root` owns visibility by default. Set `defaultOpen` for its initial state. Triggers, close controls, Escape, and outside clicks update that state.

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Dialog } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

export const AccountDialog = () => (
  <Dialog.Root defaultOpen={false}>
    <Dialog.Trigger render={<Button>Edit account</Button>} />
    <Dialog.Portal>
      <Dialog.Backdrop />
      <Dialog.Viewport>
        <Dialog.Popup>
          <Dialog.Header>
            <Dialog.Title>Edit account</Dialog.Title>
            <Dialog.Description>Update the account details.</Dialog.Description>
          </Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Body>
            <Field.Root name="company">
              <Field.Label>Company name</Field.Label>
              <Input defaultValue="Acme" />
            </Field.Root>
          </Dialog.Body>
          <Dialog.Footer>
            <Dialog.Close render={<Button variant="outline">Close</Button>} />
            <Dialog.Close render={<Button>Save</Button>} />
          </Dialog.Footer>
        </Dialog.Popup>
      </Dialog.Viewport>
    </Dialog.Portal>
  </Dialog.Root>
);
```

## Anatomy

```text
Dialog.Root
├── Dialog.Trigger
└── Dialog.Portal
    ├── Dialog.Backdrop
    └── Dialog.Viewport
        └── Dialog.Popup
            ├── Dialog.Header
            │   ├── Dialog.Title
            │   └── Dialog.Description
            ├── Dialog.Body
            └── Dialog.Footer
                └── Dialog.Close
```

| Part                       | Native and ref target                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                     | Coordinates visibility and modal behavior. Renders no DOM node and accepts no native attributes or DOM ref. |
| `Trigger`                  | A button by default. Opens the dialog and supplies a focus restoration target.                              |
| `Portal`                   | The portal div. Owns the destination container and whether closed content stays mounted.                    |
| `Backdrop`                 | The backdrop div beneath the popup. Optional; omit it when no visible backdrop is needed.                   |
| `Viewport`                 | The positioning div around the popup.                                                                       |
| `Popup`                    | The dialog div. Owns content, size, focus targets and dialog semantics.                                     |
| `Title`                    | An `h2` by default. Supplies the accessible name. Supply `aria-label` on `Popup` when omitting it.          |
| `Description`              | A paragraph by default. Associates supporting text with the dialog.                                         |
| `Header`, `Body`, `Footer` | Optional divs arranging headings, content and actions.                                                      |
| `Close`                    | A button by default. Provides a visible close action, including for touch screen readers.                   |

Assemble `Portal`, `Backdrop`, `Viewport` and `Popup` explicitly. Each DOM part accepts its own native attributes, handlers, `className`, `style`, ref and `render` composition. A ref targets that part's rendered element. `Popup` does not create a portal, backdrop or viewport.

## Controlled state

Pass `open` and `onOpenChange` when the application owns visibility. The callback receives the requested state and Base UI event details, including `reason`, `event`, `trigger` and `cancel()`. Update state to accept a change, or call `eventDetails.cancel()` to reject it. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs when the opening or closing animation finishes.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Dialog } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

export const AccountDialog = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Dialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <Dialog.Trigger render={<Button>Edit account</Button>} />
      <Dialog.Portal>
        <Dialog.Backdrop />
        <Dialog.Viewport>
          <Dialog.Popup>
            <Dialog.Header>
              <Dialog.Title>Edit account</Dialog.Title>
              <Dialog.Description>
                Update the account details.
              </Dialog.Description>
            </Dialog.Header>
            <Dialog.Body>
              <Field.Root name="company">
                <Field.Label>Company name</Field.Label>
                <Input defaultValue="Acme" />
              </Field.Root>
            </Dialog.Body>
            <Dialog.Footer>
              <Dialog.Close render={<Button variant="outline">Close</Button>} />
              <Dialog.Close render={<Button>Save</Button>} />
            </Dialog.Footer>
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
};
```

For an asynchronous form, keep the dialog open while submitting. Close it after success and display failures inside the dialog.

## Composition

`Trigger` and `Close` accept `render` to compose with `Button`, as shown above. Custom wrappers must [forward supplied props and refs](/ui/primitives/overview#custom-components). DOM parts preserve Base UI's state-aware class names, styles and callback `render` contracts. `Header`, `Body` and `Footer` retain their styled layout and native div composition.

Nest another `Dialog.Root` inside a popup to open a second dialog. Closing the nested dialog returns focus to its trigger in the parent.

To open one dialog from triggers outside `Root`, create a handle once with `Dialog.createHandle<TPayload>()` and pass it to `handle` on both `Root` and each `Trigger`. Trigger `payload` values are available in `Root`'s render function. `Dialog.Handle` and the public `DialogHandle` type expose the installed handle contract:

| Member                     | Purpose                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `open(triggerId)`          | Opens with a matching trigger as the active trigger.  |
| `open(null)`               | Opens without associating a trigger.                  |
| `openWithPayload(payload)` | Opens with a typed payload and no associated trigger. |
| `close()`                  | Requests closure.                                     |
| `isOpen`                   | Reads whether the associated dialog is open.          |

Imperative actions take effect only while the associated Root is mounted. Root's `actionsRef` also exposes `close()` and `unmount()` for explicit transition control. To control an external closing animation, call `eventDetails.preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange`, then call the `unmount()` action when the animation finishes.

`Title` uses `Heading` and defaults to an `h2` with large type, primary text color, centered alignment, and spacing-4 below it. Use `level` to change the heading level independently of `size`, or `color` to change its text color. Native `className`, `style`, refs, and `render` are forwarded to the heading. Keep a heading element when using `render`. `Description` is centered like `Title`; AlertDialog keeps both left-aligned.

`Popup` has no padding. `Header`, `Body` and `Footer` provide the inset, so content placed directly in `Popup` sits against its edges.

## Focus, scrolling, and dismissal

`Root.modal` controls the interaction boundary:

| Value            | Focus                     | Page scrolling and outside interaction                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true` (default) | Trapped inside the dialog | Page scrolling and outside interaction are blocked.      |
| `"trap-focus"`   | Trapped inside the dialog | Page scrolling and outside interaction remain available. |
| `false`          | Can leave the dialog      | Page scrolling and outside interaction remain available. |

Omit `Backdrop` when no visible backdrop is needed. For a nonmodal dialog whose viewport should pass pointer events through to the page, use `<Dialog.Viewport data-backdrop-hidden="true">`; Popup remains interactive. Omitting the visual backdrop alone does not change `Root.modal`.

Set `Popup.initialFocus` or `Popup.finalFocus` to a ref or callback to choose focus targets; `false` disables that automatic focus move. Focus callbacks receive the interaction type and retain Base UI's boolean, element, null and undefined return behavior. Closing normally restores focus to the trigger or previously focused element.

`Root.disablePointerDismissal` prevents outside clicks from requesting closure. To prevent Escape dismissal, cancel the `escape-key` change in `onOpenChange`. Always provide a visible way to close a modal dialog.

## Sizes and portals

`Popup.size` accepts `sm`, `compact`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `fullscreen`, and defaults to `md`. Long content scrolls within the popup. Width is constrained to the viewport.

Set `Portal.container` to choose a destination:

| Value                   | Resolution                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Omitted or `undefined`  | Uses the nearest scoped theme container. Without one, Base UI uses the parent portal or document body.                    |
| Element or `ShadowRoot` | Uses that explicit destination instead of the theme scope.                                                                |
| Ref                     | Base UI resolves its current element. A ref whose current value is null falls back to the parent portal or document body. |
| `null`                  | Waits without mounting. Supply a destination in a later render to mount.                                                  |

`Portal.keepMounted` retains content and form state while closed. `Viewport` and `Popup` carry the provided text direction into an external container; their explicit `dir` props take precedence. Without a direction provider or explicit `dir`, they inherit from the destination. See [theming](/ui/theming) and [DirectionProvider](/ui/primitives/layout/direction-provider).

Customize `Backdrop` and `Viewport` through their own props. Their native attributes, handlers, refs and `render` apply to those elements independently of Popup. Backdrop's `forceRender` keeps a nested dialog's backdrop visible when needed. Base UI open and transition state remains available to state-aware styles and render callbacks.

## Migration

Wrap existing `Dialog.Popup` content in `Dialog.Portal` and `Dialog.Viewport`, and add a sibling `Dialog.Backdrop` inside Portal. Move `container` and `keepMounted` from Popup to Portal. Move former `backdrop` props onto Backdrop; replace `backdrop={false}` by omitting Backdrop. Move `viewportProps` onto Viewport, retaining `data-backdrop-hidden="true"` when the viewport must pass outside pointer events through. Keep `size`, `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, native popup attributes and popup refs on Popup. The fused Popup assembly props are removed.

Root, Trigger, Close, Title, Description, Header, Body, Footer and existing handles retain their roles. Public part props, state, actions and event-detail types are exported from `twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces`.

## Props

<DialogReference />

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-overlays" />

props.name: actionsRef
props.description:
A ref to imperative actions.
- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the dialog after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the dialog completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the dialog imperatively when called.

props.name: children
props.description: Parts or a render function receiving the active trigger payload. Root renders no DOM node.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the dialog is initially open.

To render a controlled dialog, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description:
ID of the trigger that the dialog is associated with.
This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open dialog.

props.name: disablePointerDismissal
props.description:
Whether to prevent the dialog from closing on outside presses.
For non-modal dialogs, this also prevents the dialog from closing when focus moves outside of it.

props.name: handle
props.description: Connects detached triggers and imperative dialog actions.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the dialog enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to just the dialog: focus is trapped, document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.
- `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the dialog, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

When `modal` is `true` or `'trap-focus'`, render `<Dialog.Close>` inside `<Dialog.Popup>` so
touch screen readers can escape the popup.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives the requested state and Base UI event details, including reason, event, trigger and cancel().

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the dialog is opened or closed.

---
title: AlertDialog
description: Ask for confirmation before an action that needs an explicit decision.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import AlertDialogReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/surfaces/alert-dialog.mdx';

## Overview

Use `AlertDialog` for a decision that interrupts the current workflow, such as confirming deletion. It provides `alertdialog` semantics, focus management, and explicit confirmation or cancellation.

This primitive is for standalone Twenty UI and host-owned interfaces. Front components must request a confirmation through the [SDK host dialog API](/developers/extend/apps/layout/front-components#host-communication-api). Direct `Dialog`, `AlertDialog`, and native browser dialogs are prohibited inside the front component renderer.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-surfaces-alertdialog--display"
  title="AlertDialog example"
  height={440}
/>

## Usage

### Uncontrolled state

Use `defaultOpen` to set the initial visibility. The dialog owns subsequent changes from its trigger, close controls, and dismissal interactions.

```tsx
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { AlertDialog } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

type DeleteConfirmationProps = { onDelete: () => void };

export const DeleteConfirmation = ({ onDelete }: DeleteConfirmationProps) => (
  <AlertDialog.Root defaultOpen={false}>
    <AlertDialog.Trigger
      render={<Button variant="solid">Delete record</Button>}
    />
    <AlertDialog.Portal>
      <AlertDialog.Backdrop />
      <AlertDialog.Viewport>
        <AlertDialog.Popup>
          <AlertDialog.Header>
            <AlertDialog.Title>Delete this record?</AlertDialog.Title>
            <AlertDialog.Description>
              This record will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be
              undone.
            </AlertDialog.Description>
          </AlertDialog.Header>
          <AlertDialog.Footer>
            <AlertDialog.Close render={<Button>Cancel</Button>} />
            <AlertDialog.Close
              onClick={onDelete}
              render={<Button color="danger">Delete</Button>}
            />
          </AlertDialog.Footer>
        </AlertDialog.Popup>
      </AlertDialog.Viewport>
    </AlertDialog.Portal>
  </AlertDialog.Root>
);
```

`defaultOpen` defaults to `false`, so it can be omitted. This example uses a synchronous confirmation callback and closes after the action runs.

## Anatomy

Keep related parts inside `AlertDialog.Root`, or connect detached triggers through a handle. Compose the portal, backdrop, viewport, and popup separately.

```text
AlertDialog.Root
├── AlertDialog.Trigger
└── AlertDialog.Portal
    ├── AlertDialog.Backdrop
    └── AlertDialog.Viewport
        └── AlertDialog.Popup
            ├── AlertDialog.Header
            │   ├── AlertDialog.Title
            │   └── AlertDialog.Description
            ├── AlertDialog.Body
            └── AlertDialog.Footer
                ├── AlertDialog.Close
                └── Confirmation action
```

| Part                       | Requirement                                   | Purpose                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                     | Required                                      | Coordinates open state and modal behavior.                              |
| `Trigger`                  | Optional for a programmatically opened dialog | Opens the dialog and provides a return focus target.                    |
| `Portal`                   | Recommended                                   | Moves the overlay to its container and controls mounting.               |
| `Backdrop`                 | Optional                                      | Visually separates the alert from the surrounding page.                 |
| `Viewport`                 | Recommended                                   | Positions the popup and provides its scrollable surrounding area.       |
| `Popup`                    | Required                                      | Renders the alert content with focus management.                        |
| `Title`                    | Recommended                                   | Supplies the visible alert name. An accessible name is always required. |
| `Description`              | Recommended for a confirmation                | Explains the decision and its consequences.                             |
| `Header`, `Body`, `Footer` | Optional layout parts                         | Arrange headings, additional content, and actions.                      |
| `Close`                    | Recommended for cancellation                  | Supplies an explicit close action.                                      |

Set `container` and `keepMounted` on `Portal`, backdrop attributes on `Backdrop`, layout attributes on `Viewport`, and `size` and focus props on `Popup`. Each element part accepts its own native attributes, handlers, ref, and `render` composition. `Popup.ref` points to the alert content element. `Title` and `Description` establish the accessible relationships; provide `aria-label` on `Popup` when omitting a title.

The confirmation action is application content, not an exported part. Use `Close` with a synchronous handler or a `Button` with controlled open state for asynchronous confirmation.

## Controlled state

Pass `open` and update it with `onOpenChange` to own the same dialog's visibility in React state. The callback receives the requested boolean and upstream event details, including `reason`, `event`, and `cancel()`. Call `eventDetails.cancel()` to reject a requested change. `onOpenChangeComplete` runs after opening or closing transitions finish.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { AlertDialog } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

type DeleteConfirmationProps = { onDelete: () => void };

export const DeleteConfirmation = ({ onDelete }: DeleteConfirmationProps) => {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <AlertDialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <AlertDialog.Trigger
        render={<Button variant="solid">Delete record</Button>}
      />
      <AlertDialog.Portal>
        <AlertDialog.Backdrop />
        <AlertDialog.Viewport>
          <AlertDialog.Popup>
            <AlertDialog.Header>
              <AlertDialog.Title>Delete this record?</AlertDialog.Title>
              <AlertDialog.Description>
                This record will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be
                undone.
              </AlertDialog.Description>
            </AlertDialog.Header>
            <AlertDialog.Footer>
              <AlertDialog.Close render={<Button>Cancel</Button>} />
              <AlertDialog.Close
                onClick={onDelete}
                render={<Button color="danger">Delete</Button>}
              />
            </AlertDialog.Footer>
          </AlertDialog.Popup>
        </AlertDialog.Viewport>
      </AlertDialog.Portal>
    </AlertDialog.Root>
  );
};
```

For asynchronous confirmation, use a `Button` with your action handler instead of `AlertDialog.Close`. Keep `open` true while the action is pending, call `setOpen(false)` after it succeeds, and show an error inside the dialog if it fails.

## Compose with buttons

Use `render` to give the trigger and close controls Twenty UI button styling. The dialog parts supply their interaction handlers and refs to the buttons.

```tsx
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { AlertDialog } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces';

type DeleteConfirmationProps = { onDelete: () => void };

export const DeleteConfirmation = ({ onDelete }: DeleteConfirmationProps) => (
  <AlertDialog.Root>
    <AlertDialog.Trigger
      render={<Button variant="solid">Delete record</Button>}
    />
    <AlertDialog.Portal>
      <AlertDialog.Backdrop />
      <AlertDialog.Viewport>
        <AlertDialog.Popup>
          <AlertDialog.Header>
            <AlertDialog.Title>Delete this record?</AlertDialog.Title>
            <AlertDialog.Description>
              This record will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be
              undone.
            </AlertDialog.Description>
          </AlertDialog.Header>
          <AlertDialog.Footer>
            <AlertDialog.Close render={<Button>Cancel</Button>} />
            <AlertDialog.Close
              onClick={onDelete}
              render={<Button color="danger">Delete</Button>}
            />
          </AlertDialog.Footer>
        </AlertDialog.Popup>
      </AlertDialog.Viewport>
    </AlertDialog.Portal>
  </AlertDialog.Root>
);
```

Keep each action as a single interactive control. If you wrap `Button` in your own component, [forward the supplied props and ref](/ui/primitives/overview#custom-components).

## Detached triggers and imperative actions

Create a handle once with `AlertDialog.createHandle<Payload>()` and pass it to `handle` on `Root` and each detached `Trigger`. A trigger's typed `payload` is available to the root's child render function. A handle also supports `open(triggerId)`, `openWithPayload(payload)`, `close()`, and the `isOpen` getter while its root is mounted. Pass a matching trigger ID to `open`, or `null` to open without a trigger. Call imperative methods from event handlers or effects.

`Root.actionsRef` exposes `close()` and `unmount()`. For an externally controlled closing animation, call `eventDetails.preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange`, then call `actionsRef.current?.unmount()` after the animation finishes. The regular styled parts manage their own transitions without these imperative actions.

## Sizing and portals

`Popup.size` accepts `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `fullscreen`, and defaults to `md`. Size and appearance belong to the AlertDialog surface and do not have to match Dialog presets.

`Portal.container` defaults to the nearest theme's portal container. Without one, Base UI uses its default portal destination, normally `document.body`. An explicit element, shadow root, or ref overrides that destination. An explicit `null` defers mounting until a container is available. Base UI resolves a ref whose `current` is `null` using its default destination; use `container={null}` when mounting must wait.

Portaled content retains the theme context. `Portal` and `Viewport` inherit the provided text direction unless you set `dir` explicitly. Set `Portal.keepMounted` to retain mounted content and form state while closed.

## Focus and dismissal

The alert traps focus, blocks outside interaction, and locks page scrolling while open. Escape requests closure; clicking outside does not. To prevent Escape dismissal, cancel the `escape-key` change in `onOpenChange`. Always provide a visible Cancel or Close action.

By default, focus moves to the first tabbable control, or to the popup for a touch opening. Put the least destructive action first, or use `Popup.initialFocus` to select it. Focus returns to the trigger or previously focused element when the alert closes. Use `Popup.finalFocus` when a successful action removes that target. Both focus props accept a boolean, element ref, or interaction-type callback according to the upstream contract.

## Props

The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

--- title: Popover description: Display contextual content anchored to a trigger. --- import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx" import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx'; import PopoverReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/surfaces/popover.mdx'; ## Overview Use `Popover` for contextual information or lightweight controls. Compose its portal, positioning wrapper and popup separately. Use [Dropdown](/ui/components/navigation/dropdown) for menus, pickers and panels with higher-level navigation. ## Usage ### Uncontrolled state Use `defaultOpen` to set the initial visibility. The popover owns subsequent changes from its trigger, close controls, and dismissal interactions. ```tsx import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; import { Popover } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces'; export const ContactDetailsPopover = () => ( Show details} /> Contact details Reach Alex at alex@example.com. Close} /> ); ``` `defaultOpen` defaults to `false`, so it can be omitted. Use `Title` and `Description` to identify the popup. The trigger renders a button by default; `render` lets you supply a compatible element. ## Placement comparison Compare the supported sides with and without an arrow. These open examples keep each popup beside its trigger for inspection; use the Display example to try opening and dismissing a popover. ## Anatomy Keep the trigger and popup inside `Popover.Root`. The popup can contain text, form controls, and actions. ```text Popover.Root ├── Popover.Trigger └── Popover.Portal ├── Popover.Backdrop (optional) └── Popover.Positioner └── Popover.Popup ├── Popover.Arrow (optional) └── Popover.Viewport (optional) ├── Popover.Title ├── Popover.Description └── Popover.Close ``` | Part | Purpose and native target | | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Root` | Owns state, triggers and interactions. Renders no DOM element. | | `Trigger` | Opens the popup and supplies its default anchor. Targets a button. | | `Portal` | Chooses the destination. Native props, handlers, `render` and ref target its div. | | `Positioner` | Owns anchors, alignment, offsets and collision handling. Targets its div. | | `Popup` | Renders content and manages focus. Targets its div. | | `Arrow` | Optional styled arrow inside Popup. Targets its div. | | `Backdrop` | Optional upstream backdrop inside Portal. Targets its div. | | `Viewport` | Optional transition container for changing content. Targets its div. | | `Title` | Supplies a visible accessible name. Targets an h2. | | `Description` | Associates explanatory text. Targets a paragraph. | | `Close` | Requests closing. Targets a button. | All rendered parts support the installed Base UI native attributes, handlers, refs and element/function `render` composition. Custom components must forward the supplied props and ref. Every part has a public `PopoverProps` and `PopoverState` type. `PopoverRootProps` and `PopoverTriggerProps` preserve payload generics. `PopoverHandle`, `PopoverRootActions`, `PopoverRootChangeEventDetails` and `PopoverRootChangeEventReason` are also exported from `twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces`. ## Controlled state Pass `open` and update it with `onOpenChange` to own the same popover's visibility in React state. ```tsx import { useState } from 'react'; import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; import { Popover } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces'; export const ContactDetailsPopover = () => { const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); return ( Show details} /> Contact details Reach Alex at alex@example.com. Close} /> ); }; ``` `onOpenChange` receives the next boolean and event details, including changes requested by the trigger, close controls, Escape, and outside interaction. ## Compose with buttons Pass a Twenty UI `Button` through `render` to use it as the trigger or close control. The popover keeps its open state, keyboard behavior, and focus handling. ```tsx import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input'; import { Popover } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces'; export const ImportHelp = () => ( Import help} /> Import a CSV file Use a header row to identify your columns. Got it} /> ); ``` `render` composes behavior onto the supplied button. Custom wrapper components must [forward the supplied props and ref](/ui/primitives/overview#custom-components) to preserve that behavior. ## Placement and focus `Positioner` defaults to `side="bottom"`, `align="center"` and `sideOffset={8}`. It accepts the full installed Base UI contract, including element/ref/function/virtual anchors, functional offsets, `positionMethod`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `arrowPadding`, `sticky` and `disableAnchorTracking`. DirectionProvider controls logical positioning and supplies the DOM direction. An explicit `dir` can override the native attribute; use the provider to change logical side placement. ```tsx import { useRef } from 'react'; import { Popover } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces'; export const AnchoredHelp = () => { const anchor = useRef(null); return (
Help anchor.width / 2} collisionBoundary="clipping-ancestors" collisionAvoidance={{ side: 'flip', align: 'shift' }} collisionPadding={8} positionMethod="fixed" > Contextual help
); }; ``` Escape closes the popup and restores focus to its trigger. Outside interaction dismisses it by default. `Popup.initialFocus` and `Popup.finalFocus` accept the upstream focus targets and callbacks. `Root.modal` retains Base UI's nonmodal default, modal and trap-focus modes for standalone usage. ## Portal destinations and theme Set `container` and `keepMounted` on `Portal`: | Container | Resolution | | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Omitted or `undefined` | Uses the nearest scoped ThemeProvider container. Without one, Base UI uses its parent portal or document body. | | `null` | Waits without rendering portal content until the container changes. It does not fall back to the theme or body. | | Element, ShadowRoot or ref | Passes the supplied target unchanged to Base UI. An unresolved ref retains Base UI's parent-portal/body fallback; use explicit null when waiting is required. | The default scoped destination preserves its CSS tokens and color scheme. An explicit destination inherits CSS from its actual DOM scope. Put it inside the intended theme scope, or supply the theme styles there. ShadowRoot targets need the library's CSS and theme styles in that shadow tree. React theme context and provided text direction remain available across portals. This API does not expand the renderer's permitted portal destinations. ## Detached triggers and payloads `Popover.createHandle()` connects detached triggers to a root and exposes `open(triggerId)`, `close()` and `isOpen`. `Popover.Handle` is the installed upstream handle constructor. Root's render function receives the active payload. Call imperative actions from event handlers or effects. ```tsx import { useState } from 'react'; import { Popover } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces'; export const OwnerHelp = () => { const [handle] = useState(() => Popover.createHandle<{ name: string }>()); return ( <> Owner {({ payload }) => ( {payload?.name} Close )} ); }; ``` `onOpenChange` preserves `reason`, `event`, `trigger`, `cancel()` and `preventUnmountOnClose()`. Controlled roots retain `triggerId`; uncontrolled roots retain `defaultTriggerId`. `actionsRef` exposes the upstream close/unmount actions. ## Migration Move `container` and `keepMounted` from Popup to Portal. Move placement, anchor and collision props to Positioner. Replace `Popup.arrow` with an explicit `Popover.Arrow` child. Popup's native props, handlers, focus props and ref continue to target the content element. Dropdown.Content keeps its existing convenient assembly. Inside front components, use nonmodal composition within the existing scoped portal policy. Native browser popovers/dialogs and direct app-owned modality are prohibited; use the SDK host dialog API for dialogs. Renderer portal, geometry, scrolling and dismissal capability work remains separate from this primitive API. ## Props The reference is generated from the public component types. Native attributes, including accessible names and event handlers, are also accepted on parts that render elements.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the popover enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the popover: document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.
- `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the popover, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

When `modal` is `true`, focus trapping is enabled only if `<Popover.Close>` is rendered
inside `<Popover.Popup>`. It can be visually hidden with your own CSS if needed, such as
Tailwind's `sr-only` utility.

When `modal` is `'trap-focus'`, render `<Popover.Close>` inside `<Popover.Popup>` so touch
screen readers can escape the popup.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

pages.content: --- title: Text description: Compose theme typography with single-line truncation or a limited number of lines. --- import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx" import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx'; import TextReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/typography/text.mdx'; ## Overview `Text` provides typography and overflow handling. It renders a `div` by default. Omit `size`, `weight` and `color` to keep inheriting typography from its surroundings. ## Usage Give the text a constrained width, then set `truncate` to show an ellipsis when it overflows: ```tsx import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography'; export const ContactName = () => ( Alexandra Montgomery ); ``` ## Choose typography `size` uses the existing theme scale. It changes font size, with no height, font-family or line-height default: | Size | Theme value | | ----- | ----------- | | `xxs` | `0.625rem` | | `xs` | `0.85rem` | | `sm` | `0.92rem` | | `md` | `1rem` | | `lg` | `1.23rem` | | `xl` | `1.54rem` | | `xxl` | `1.85rem` | `weight` accepts `regular` (400), `medium` (500) or `semibold` (600). `color` accepts `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary` or `light`. Each omitted prop inherits independently. The visual size does not change the semantic element. For captions, compose the small size, semibold weight and light color: ```tsx import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography'; export const Caption = () => ( Workspace ); ``` Use native `style` for runtime colors and parent-layout constraints. Caller classes and render composition target the same text element. Text adds no typography defaults when these props are omitted. ## Limit the number of lines Use `lineClamp` with a positive integer. Choose either `truncate` or `lineClamp`; their props are mutually exclusive. ```tsx import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography'; export const Summary = () => ( Follow up with the customer about their onboarding milestones and upcoming renewal. ); ``` ## Choose an element Use `render` when the text needs another semantic element: ```tsx import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography'; export const Description = () => ( }>Account description ); ``` Truncation affects the visual presentation; it does not shorten the text in the DOM. Provide a way to read the full content when the visible portion is insufficient. ## Props Native attributes, children, refs, class names, and styles target the rendered text element. `TextProps` is exported from `twenty-ui/primitives/typography`. Text content is rendered unchanged, including caller-provided links. ## Migration `color` now selects a semantic theme color. Move arbitrary CSS color values from a native `color` attribute to `style={{ color: customColor }}`. Existing styles, classes and render composition continue to target the text element.

---
title: Heading
description: Render semantic headings with independent visual sizes.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import HeadingReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/typography/heading.mdx';

## Overview

`Heading` renders an `h2` by default. Use `children` for its content, `level` for document structure, and `size` for appearance.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-heading--display"
  title="Heading example"
  height={90}
/>

## Usage

Choose levels in document order. A smaller visual size does not change the level announced by assistive technology.

```tsx
import { Heading } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const WorkspaceTitle = () => <Heading>Workspace settings</Heading>;
```

Sizes `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, and `xxl` use the matching font tokens. The larger sizes use `1.54rem` and `1.85rem`, respectively. All sizes keep semibold weight and a `1.1` line height. `Section.Header` and `Dialog.Title` accept the same size values. Headings have no outer margin; their surrounding layout owns spacing.

## Color and composition

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-typography-heading--catalog"
  title="Heading sizes and colors"
  height={480}
/>

Use `color="secondary"` for less prominent headings. `tertiary` is also available, but its contrast depends on the font size, theme, and background. Check readability when using it.

Native attributes, styles, class names, and refs pass to the heading. Use `render` to compose with a custom element or component; that element is responsible for preserving heading semantics.

For a heading with supporting text or actions, use [Section](/ui/components/layout/section).

## Props

<HeadingReference />

<PageBanner illustration="section-document-generator" />

---
title: LabeledSeparator
description: Separate content with a centered or end-aligned text label.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import LabeledSeparatorReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/layout/labeled-separator.mdx';

## Overview

`LabeledSeparator` composes [Separator](/ui/primitives/layout/separator) and [Text](/ui/primitives/typography/text) into a named horizontal divider. Your application supplies the label and surrounding spacing.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-labeledseparator--display"
  title="Labeled separator between import options"
  height={180}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { LabeledSeparator } from 'twenty-ui/components/layout';
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const ImportOptions = () => (
  <Text
    style={{
      display: 'grid',
      gap: 'var(--t-spacing-3)',
      width: 320,
      maxWidth: '100%',
    }}
  >
    <Button fullWidth>Import a CSV file</Button>
    <LabeledSeparator>Or</LabeledSeparator>
    <Button fullWidth variant="outline">
      Connect a data source
    </Button>
  </Text>
);
```

## Label placement and tone

`labelPosition` defaults to `center`, with a line on each side of the label. Use `end` to place the label after the leading line. The label accepts a string supplied and localized by your application.

`tone` defaults to `neutral`. Use `danger` for a red marker with a medium-weight label and a thicker rule. Set `hasStartMarker` to add a small decorative cap at the beginning of the rule.

The optional cap follows the [shared calendar and chat line design](https://www.figma.com/design/xt8O9mFeLl46C5InWwoMrN/Twenty?node-id=118289-146574).

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-layout-labeledseparator--unread-marker"
  title="Unread marker with an end-aligned label"
  height={100}
/>

```tsx
import { LabeledSeparator } from 'twenty-ui/components/layout';

export const UnreadMarker = () => (
  <LabeledSeparator
    labelPosition="end"
    tone="danger"
    hasStartMarker
    style={{ width: 488, maxWidth: '100%' }}
  >
    New
  </LabeledSeparator>
);
```

## Spacing and application state

The component fills its container and adds no outer margin. Use parent layout spacing or native `style` and `className` for margins and alignment. Keep offsets for adjacent avatars or calendar positions in your application.

The component presents the supplied label. Your application decides where an unread boundary or calendar marker belongs and when it is visible.

## Accessibility and composition

The root exposes one horizontal separator named from its label. The rule segments and optional start marker are decorative, so assistive technology does not announce extra separators. Native accessible attributes can provide a different name or description when needed.

Native attributes, styles, class names, and `ref` target the outer `div`. Use `render` to compose another noninteractive element while forwarding the supplied props and ref. `LabeledSeparatorProps` is exported from `twenty-ui/components/layout`.

## Migration

Replace the frontend `LabeledDivider` with `LabeledSeparator`. Rename `textPosition` to `labelPosition`, and use `tone="danger"` for the unread marker's red appearance. Remove `noMargin`, since outer margins default to zero. Preserve the former default spacing with `style={{ marginBlock: 'var(--t-spacing-3)' }}` where needed.

## Props

<LabeledSeparatorReference />

<PageBanner illustration="layout" />

props.description: Text naming the separator. Supplied and localized by the caller.

props.name: hasStartMarker
props.description: Show a decorative cap at the beginning of the rule.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Place the label between two lines or at the end of one line.

props.name: render
props.description:
Allows you to replace the component's HTML element
with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: tone
props.description: Neutral divider or red marker with a thicker rule.

pages.name: Section
pages.content:
---
title: Section
description: Group content with a heading, supporting description, and optional action.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import SectionReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/layout/section.mdx';

## Overview

`Section.Root` groups related content. `Section.Header` combines [Heading](/ui/primitives/typography/heading) with a description and optional `actions` content. Descriptions are ordinary text associated with the heading, so they do not add levels to the document outline.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-section--display"
  title="Section example"
  height={150}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { Section } from 'twenty-ui/components/layout';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const WorkspaceSection = () => (
  <Section.Root>
    <Section.Header
      title="Workspace settings"
      description="Manage your workspace name and preferences."
    />
    <Text>Workspace preferences appear here.</Text>
  </Section.Root>
);
```

## Add a description and action

```tsx
import { Section } from 'twenty-ui/components/layout';
import { Button } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const WorkspaceSection = () => (
  <Section.Root>
    <Section.Header
      title="Workspace settings"
      description="Manage your workspace name and preferences."
      actions={<Button>Edit workspace</Button>}
    />
    <Text>Workspace preferences appear here.</Text>
  </Section.Root>
);
```

`Section.Root` defaults to a full-width `div` with left alignment and the primary text color. Use `align`, `color`, and `fullWidth` to adjust the content wrapper.

`Section.Header` can also be used by itself. Its `level`, `size`, and `color` configure the heading and default to `2`, `md`, and `primary`. The header has one spacing-4 margin after it. Use native `style` or `className` to adjust that spacing.

## Description overflow

String descriptions show up to five lines. Set `descriptionLineClamp` to a positive integer to choose another limit, or `false` to display the full description without an overflow tooltip. Hover reveals overflowing text. Descriptions do not add a tab stop by default; set `isDescriptionFocusable` to enable focus access to the tooltip. Escape dismisses the tooltip.

The heading accepts node content. Choose `level` for the document outline independently of visual `size` and `color`. Compose links and other rich content explicitly in a node description.

Pass a React node for richer supporting content. Rich descriptions render as supplied, without automatic truncation or tooltips.

## Composition

Both parts forward native attributes, refs, class names, styles, and `render` to their outer element. For example, `Section.Root render={<section aria-label="Workspace settings" />}` provides a named section, and `Section.Header render={<header />}` uses a header container.

When migrating, replace `adornment` with `actions`. Opt into description focus with `isDescriptionFocusable` when needed. `SectionRootProps` and `SectionHeaderProps` are exported from `twenty-ui/components/layout`.

pages.name: AssistantAvatar
pages.content:
---
title: AssistantAvatar
description: An assistant character with configurable shape, expression, color, size, and idle animation.
---

import { PageBanner } from '/snippets/page-banner.mdx';

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import AssistantAvatarReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/data-display/assistant-avatar.mdx';

## Overview

Render an assistant character from a body shape, face, palette color, and size. The component displays the supplied values; your application owns selection and persistence.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-data-display-assistantavatar--display"
  title="Assistant character beside its name"
  height={100}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { AssistantAvatar } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';
import { Text } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/typography';

export const AssistantLabel = () => (
  <Text style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <AssistantAvatar shape="circle" face="default" color="blue" size={24} />
    <Text>Workspace assistant</Text>
  </Text>
);
```

## Visual options

Choose shapes independently from expressions and colors.

| Prop         | Values                                                                                     | Default   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| `shape`      | `circle`, `cookie`, `cloud`, `clover`, `flower`, `burst`, `pill`, `arch`, `gem`, `hexagon` | `circle`  |
| `face`       | `default`, `happy`, `wink`, `surprised`, `sleepy`, `love`                                  | `default` |
| `color`      | `blue`, `sky`, `turquoise`, `green`, `yellow`, `orange`, `red`, `pink`, `purple`, `gray`   | `blue`    |
| `size`       | `14`, `16`, `20`, `24`, `40` pixels                                                        | `24`      |
| `isAnimated` | `true`, `false`                                                                            | `false`   |

The body and face use the selected palette's theme tokens and follow the surrounding light or dark theme. Set `size` for a square character. Native attributes, events, `className`, `style`, and `ref` target the outer span; explicit styles override its dimensions and palette defaults.

```tsx
import { AssistantAvatar } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';

export const CustomAssistant = () => (
  <AssistantAvatar
    shape="cloud"
    face="happy"
    color="sky"
    size={40}
    aria-label="Workspace assistant"
  />
);
```

## Idle animation

Set `isAnimated` to play the selected expression's idle loop. Default blinks and glances sideways, Happy lifts its eyes, Wink closes one eye, Surprised widens its eyes, Sleepy floats a sleep mark, and Love pulses its heart eyes. The body stays still.

```tsx
import { AssistantAvatar } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';

export const AnimatedAssistant = () => (
  <AssistantAvatar face="happy" isAnimated aria-label="Workspace assistant" />
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-components-data-display-assistantavatar--idle-faces"
  title="Idle animations for each expression"
  height={180}
/>

Animation is off by default. Set `isAnimated={false}` to display the static expression, including the visible wink. When the browser prefers reduced motion, the component displays the static expression even when `isAnimated` is enabled. The preference also applies if it changes while the character is displayed.

The application owns the animation toggle. This prop controls idle presentation and does not represent listening, speaking, thinking, or other assistant activity.

## Accessibility

The character is decorative when it has no accessible name, as in the labeled Usage example. For a standalone character, supply `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; the root then exposes the image role. The body and face stay hidden from assistive technology so the character is announced once.

Set `aria-hidden` explicitly when you need to override the name-based default, such as hiding a named character beside equivalent visible text.

Place the character inside a named button or link when it accompanies an action. The application owns the control, its label, and its behavior.

<PageBanner illustration="page-cover-assistant-avatar" />

pages.name: JsonTree
pages.content:
---
title: JsonTree
description: Explore JSON values with expandable nodes and custom labels.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';

import JsonTreeReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/data-display/json-tree.mdx';

## Overview

`JsonTree` displays either a JSON `value` or an array of named `entries`. Pass all empty-value and expand/collapse labels so your application controls the text.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-jsonvisualizer-jsontree--display"
  title="Expandable record details"
  height={320}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { JsonTree } from 'twenty-ui/components/data-display';

export const RecordDetails = () => (
  <JsonTree
    value={{ name: 'Acme', active: true, contacts: [] }}
    emptyStringLabel="Empty text"
    emptyArrayLabel="No items"
    emptyObjectLabel="No properties"
    arrowButtonCollapsedLabel="Expand node"
    arrowButtonExpandedLabel="Collapse node"
  />
);
```

Each entry has an `id`, `label`, and JSON `value`. Use entries when display labels differ from stored keys. The default expands depths 0 and 1. Override `shouldExpandNodeInitially={({ depth }) => depth === 0}` to expand only the root; later expansion is owned by each node.

`getNodeHighlighting(keyPath)` returns `blue`, `red`, `partial-blue`, or `undefined`. `onNodeValueClick` receives the displayed text: leaf values as strings, and the matching empty label for empty strings, arrays, and objects. The tree displays data and does not edit it.

When `onNodeValueClick` is provided, values are native buttons named by their displayed text. Tab moves focus to a value; Enter, Space, or a pointer click activates it. Without the callback, values remain non-interactive text. Value buttons do not submit enclosing forms.

---
title: InlineBanner
description: Inline feedback with node content, icons, and actions.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

import { StoryEmbed } from '/snippets/ui/StoryEmbed.mdx';
import InlineBannerReference from '/snippets/ui/generated/components/feedback/inline-banner.mdx';

## Overview

`InlineBanner` composes [Banner](/ui/primitives/feedback/banner) with a rounded inline layout and a decorative information icon. It shares Banner's independent `status`, `variant`, `color`, `icon` and `action` contracts. Its default appearance is `soft` and its default status is `info`.

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-inlinebanner--display"
  title="Inline banner with an action"
  height={130}
/>

## Usage

```tsx
import { InlineBanner } from 'twenty-ui/components/feedback';

export const ModelsBanner = ({ onConfigure }: { onConfigure: () => void }) => (
  <InlineBanner
    status="error"
    action={
      <InlineBanner.Action onClick={onConfigure}>
        Configure models
      </InlineBanner.Action>
    }
  >
    No AI models are enabled.
  </InlineBanner>
);
```

The `standard` layout fills the available width. Plain string children truncate, with keyboard focus, pointer hover or touch revealing the full string in a tooltip. Rich node children render directly, so embedded links and controls retain their own semantics. Compose explicit typography when rich content needs truncation.

Use `layout="compact"` for wrapping content, closer spacing and a maximum content width of 512px. Add `fullWidth` to remove that cap and fill the available parent width, including padding and borders. It defaults to `false` and does not change the standard layout, which already fills its parent. It has no bottom margin. Layout is independent of `solid` or `soft` appearance. `embedded` removes the standard layout's bottom margin.

```tsx
import { InlineBanner } from 'twenty-ui/components/feedback';
import { IconInfoCircle } from 'twenty-ui/icon';

export const ConnectionBanner = () => (
  <InlineBanner
    layout="compact"
    status="warning"
    color="blue"
    icon={<IconInfoCircle aria-hidden="true" />}
    action={
      <InlineBanner.Action href="/settings/accounts">
        Connection settings
      </InlineBanner.Action>
    }
  >
    Connect your account to sync contacts.
  </InlineBanner>
);
```

<StoryEmbed
  storyId="ui-feedback-inlinebanner--compact-link"
  title="Compact banner with a destination link"
  height={120}
/>

`InlineBanner.Action` provides a small outline button that inherits the banner’s displayed color, including explicit palette overrides and solid appearances. It supports Button interactions, links, refs and custom rendering. The `action` slot also accepts arbitrary controls.

The root target is a `div`. Native props, `className`, `style` and `ref` target that root; Base UI `render` can compose another element and receives resolved Banner state. `action` accepts any ReactNode, including multiple controls with their complete Button or link APIs. `icon={null}` removes the default icon.

The caller owns whether the banner is rendered and whether changes should be announced. Supply `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`, or an appropriate live-region wrapper, when needed. Status does not assign live-region semantics. Name action controls and mark decorative custom icons with `aria-hidden`.

## Migration

Replace `message` with `children`, `LeftIcon={Icon}` with `icon={<Icon />}`, and `button` configuration with an `action` node. Use `InlineBanner.Action` to keep action styling aligned with the banner. Replace `variant="compact"` with `layout="compact"`; standard is now the default layout. Use `status="error"` for error meaning or `color="red"` for a palette override.

## Props

<PageBanner illustration="card-page-messaging-channels" />

---
title: Getting started
description: Install Twenty UI in a React application and use its components and themes.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

## Overview

Twenty UI is Twenty's open-source React UI library. It provides foundational primitives, shared components, icons, and theme tokens with prebuilt CSS, so your application does not need a CSS-in-JS compiler.

## Install

For an existing React application, install the library. React 19 is required.

```bash
yarn add twenty-ui
```

The [code editor](/ui/components/code-editor/code-editor) has a separate entry point, `twenty-ui/components/code-editor`. Other components do not require Monaco. To use the code editor, install its optional peer dependencies and configure Monaco workers for your bundler before mounting it:

```bash
yarn add @monaco-editor/react monaco-editor
```

If you are building a Twenty app, follow [Using Twenty UI components](/developers/extend/apps/layout/front-components#using-twenty-ui-components). The front component renderer supplies the workspace theme and has a different setup from a standalone browser application. Keep `twenty-ui`, `twenty-sdk`, and `twenty-client-sdk` on the same version.

## Load styles and provide a theme

Import the component stylesheet and a theme stylesheet once at your application entry point. `ThemeProvider` applies the active theme class and makes theme values available to components.

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';
import { ThemeProvider } from 'twenty-ui/theme';

import 'twenty-ui/style.css';
import 'twenty-ui/theme-light.css';

export const App = () => (
  <ThemeProvider colorScheme="light">
    <Field.Root>
      <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
      <Input name="email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Field.Description>Use your work email address.</Field.Description>
    </Field.Root>
  </ThemeProvider>
);
```

The component stylesheet includes a global reset. Review its effect when adding Twenty UI to an existing application.

## Override styles

Twenty UI puts component styles and the reset in the `twenty-ui` cascade layer. Styles you write outside a layer, such as a `className`, a CSS module, or a CSS-in-JS rule, override those layered rules regardless of selector specificity or import order. Theme stylesheets and the optional editor's global Monaco rules remain unlayered.

Global element resets in your application are unlayered too, so they would override Twenty UI components. Declare a layer for them before Twenty UI's stylesheet loads:

```css
@layer reset, twenty-ui;

@layer reset {
  button {
    font: inherit;
  }
}
```

With Tailwind CSS v4, place Twenty UI between Tailwind's base and utility layers:

```css
@layer theme, base, twenty-ui, components, utilities;
```

## Choose an entry point

Import components from their public subpath to keep imports focused:

Primitives are foundational controls, including compound controls such as Select,
Popover, and AlertDialog. Shared components combine primitives into recurring
design presets and reusable app building blocks. Both receive data and callbacks
from the application.

Use [MainButton](/ui/components/input/main-button) for prominent actions and
[LightButton](/ui/components/input/light-button) for lightweight actions. Both
come from `twenty-ui/components/input` and share the foundational
[Button](/ui/primitives/input/button) interaction contract. Routing and page
layout remain in the application.

Each primitive and shared component family has a matching public entry point, such as
`twenty-ui/primitives/input` and `twenty-ui/components/settings`. The aggregate
`twenty-ui/primitives` and `twenty-ui/components` entries export their respective families.
The root `twenty-ui` entry re-exports primitives, shared components, icons, theme tokens,
and utilities. Assets, testing helpers, and the optional code editor have separate entry points.

| Import                               | Contents                                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `twenty-ui/assets`                   | Logos and static assets                                             |
| `twenty-ui/components`               | All shared component families except the optional editor            |
| `twenty-ui/components/data-display`  | Avatar groups, command blocks, JSON trees, metrics, and icon tiles  |
| `twenty-ui/components/feedback`      | Callouts, inline banners, and notifications                         |
| `twenty-ui/components/input`         | Button presets, specialized inputs, pickers, and segmented controls |
| `twenty-ui/components/layout`        | Sections, overflowing lists, and icon transitions                   |
| `twenty-ui/components/navigation`    | Dropdowns, menu compositions, and tab actions                       |
| `twenty-ui/components/settings`      | Settings rows with labeled controls                                 |
| `twenty-ui/components/code-editor`   | Code editor, editor header, and editor theme helpers                |
| `twenty-ui/primitives`               | All primitive families                                              |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/accessibility` | Hidden elements and keyboard interaction helpers                    |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/data-display`  | Avatars, badges, chips, tags, color samples, and status indicators  |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/feedback`      | Banners, progress indicators, loaders, and skeletons                |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/input`         | Buttons and form controls                                           |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/layout`        | Expansion, separators, direction, and resizing                      |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/navigation`    | Breadcrumbs, list items, and tabs                                   |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/surfaces`      | Cards, dialogs, popovers, and tooltips                              |
| `twenty-ui/primitives/typography`    | Text, headings, shortcuts, and overflowing text                     |
| `twenty-ui/icon`                     | [Icons and dynamic lookup](/ui/icons)                               |
| `twenty-ui/testing`                  | [Storybook decorators and layouts](/ui/testing)                     |
| `twenty-ui/theme`                    | Theme provider, hooks, and CSS variable references                  |
| `twenty-ui/utilities`                | Hooks and shared utilities                                          |

Import individual icons, such as `IconCheck`, from `twenty-ui/icon`. The dynamic icon provider includes the full icon catalog, so reserve it for interfaces that need to look up icons at runtime.

## Responsive hooks

Import `useIsMobile`, `useIsTouchDevice`, and `useMediaQuery` from `twenty-ui/utilities`.

| Hook                   | Query                                                             | Use                                                       |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useIsMobile()`        | `MOBILE_MEDIA_QUERY`, up to and including `MOBILE_VIEWPORT`       | Choose a compact layout.                                  |
| `useIsTouchDevice()`   | `TOUCH_DEVICE_MEDIA_QUERY`, `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` | Choose touch interaction behavior independently of width. |
| `useMediaQuery(query)` | Any media query supported by `window.matchMedia`                  | Subscribe to a custom media query.                        |

The query constants come from `twenty-ui/utilities`; `MOBILE_VIEWPORT` comes from `twenty-ui/theme`. Subscriptions share one `MediaQueryList` per query and update when its match changes. Hooks return `false` during server rendering, the first hydration render, and when `window.matchMedia` is unavailable.

In a [Twenty front component](/developers/extend/apps/layout/front-components#current-limitations), width queries follow the widget's box. `useIsMobile` therefore follows the widget width, while `useIsTouchDevice` follows the device's primary input. Use [story overrides](/ui/testing#media-query-overrides) to exercise these states in Storybook.

## Continue

- [Theming](/ui/theming): use semantic tokens and scoped overrides.
- [Dark mode](/ui/dark-mode): switch between light and dark palettes.

## Browse the library

- [Primitives](/ui/primitives/overview): foundational controls grouped by family, with usage examples and API references.
- [Components](/ui/components/overview): shared design presets and reusable app building blocks composed from primitives.

---
title: Accessibility
description: Label controls, preserve keyboard behavior, and test accessible Twenty UI interfaces.
---

import { PageBanner } from "/snippets/page-banner.mdx"

## Overview

Migrated interactive components use Base UI primitives for semantics and keyboard behavior. Your application still supplies meaningful labels, descriptions, error messages, and focus order.

## Label every control

Use `Field.Label` with an input to associate a visible label with the control. `Field.Description` supplies supporting text:

```tsx
import { Field, Input } from 'twenty-ui/primitives/input';

export const EmailField = () => (
  <Field.Root>
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Input type="email" name="email" required />
    <Field.Description>
      We send account updates to this address.
    </Field.Description>
    <Field.Error>Enter a valid email address.</Field.Error>
  </Field.Root>
);
```

Use [VisuallyHidden](/ui/primitives/accessibility/visually-hidden) when supporting text should remain available to assistive technology without being displayed.

Placeholders supplement labels; they do not replace them. For a control without visible text, supply an accessible name using `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

## Preserve native behavior

Use the component's state and change props, such as `checked` and `onCheckedChange` on `Switch`. Keep focus indicators visible. When using `render` to replace an element, preserve the ref, event handlers, and attributes the component passes to it.

A disabled control cannot be changed and is generally excluded from keyboard navigation and form submission. A read-only control retains its value and may remain focusable; choose the state that matches the interaction you intend.

## Test the complete interface

Check keyboard navigation, labels, error announcements, focus movement in overlays, and zoom in the context where the component is used. Verify contrast in both palettes and after applying custom token overrides.

Twenty UI's stories contain interaction and automated accessibility checks. Some stories still defer color-contrast checks, so those checks do not establish full accessibility conformance for an application.
